# 4. Auxiliary Functions

```{r functions}
#############################################
### HELPER FUNCTIONS FOR PHYLOGENETIC ANALYSIS
#############################################
# This section contains utility functions for:
#   - File validation and format checking
#   - Taxonomic data extraction and parsing
#   - Label cleaning and standardization
#   - Metadata loading and matching
#   - Presence/absence table generation
#   - Tree statistics and validation

#############################################
### FUNCTION: Validate file existence and format
#############################################
# Verifies that input file exists and has valid Newick extension
# 
# Newick format is the standard for representing phylogenetic trees
# Common file extensions: .nwk, .newick, .tree, .tre
# 
# Parameters:
#   file_path - character string with full path to tree file
# 
# Returns:
#   logical TRUE if validation passes
# 
# Stops execution if:
#   - File does not exist at specified path
# 
# Warnings:
#   - Issues warning if file has non-standard extension
#     (but allows processing to continue)
# 
# Side effects:
#   - Prints validation confirmation message to console
# 
# Example:
#   validate_file("phylogenetic/CK/07_iqtree/LOG/LOG.nwk")

validate_file <- function(file_path) {
  # Verify file exists at specified path
  if (!file.exists(file_path)) {
    stop(paste("ERROR: File does not exist:", file_path))
  }
  
  # Check for standard Newick format extension
  # Accepts: .nwk, .newick, .tree, .tre (case-insensitive)
  if (!grepl("\\.nwk$|\\.newick$|\\.tree$|\\.tre$", file_path, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
    warning("File does not have standard Newick extension (.nwk, .newick, .tree, .tre)")
  }
  
  cat("✓ File validated:", file_path, "\n")
  return(TRUE)
}

#############################################
### FUNCTION: Validate UniProt ID format
#############################################
# Checks if a string matches UniProt accession format specifications
# 
# UniProt IDs are standardized protein database accessions with specific format:
#   - Mix of uppercase letters and numbers
#   - Length between 6-15 characters
#   - Cannot be pure numeric
#   - May contain underscores
# 
# Common formats:
#   - P12345 (Swiss-Prot entry)
#   - A0A1C7NW11 (TrEMBL entry)
#   - Q9Y6K1_HUMAN (with species suffix)
# 
# Parameters:
#   id - character string to validate
# 
# Returns:
#   logical TRUE if ID matches UniProt format, FALSE otherwise
# 
# Validation criteria:
#   1. Not empty, NA, or NULL
#   2. Contains both letters and numbers
#   3. Length is 6-15 characters
#   4. Not pure numeric string
#   5. Contains only uppercase letters, numbers, and underscores
# 
# Example:
#   is_valid_uniprot("A0A1C7NW11")  # Returns TRUE
#   is_valid_uniprot("12345")       # Returns FALSE (pure numeric)
#   is_valid_uniprot("ABC")         # Returns FALSE (too short, no numbers)

is_valid_uniprot <- function(id) {
  # Handle missing or empty values
  if (is.na(id) || id == "" || is.null(id)) return(FALSE)
  
  # Reject pure numeric strings (not valid UniProt format)
  if (grepl("^[0-9]+$", id)) return(FALSE)
  
  # Check length constraints
  # UniProt IDs are typically 6-15 characters
  if (nchar(id) < 6) return(FALSE)
  if (nchar(id) > 15) return(FALSE)
  
  # Verify presence of both letters and numbers
  has_letters <- grepl("[A-Z]", id)
  has_numbers <- grepl("[0-9]", id)
  
  # Valid if contains both letters and numbers
  # and only uses alphanumeric characters plus underscore
  if (has_letters && has_numbers && grepl("^[A-Z0-9_]+$", id)) {
    return(TRUE)
  }
  
  return(FALSE)
}

#############################################
### FUNCTION: Extract taxonomic components from tip labels
#############################################
# Parses structured tip labels to extract taxonomic and protein information
# 
# This function handles the standard output from preprocessing pipelines
# where sequences are labeled with multiple data fields separated by underscores
# 
# Expected label structure:
#   Genus_species_TaxID_UniprotID_GeneName
#   Example: Aspergillus_niger_5061_A0A1C7NW11_histidine_kinase
# 
# The function handles variable label structures:
#   - Minimum: Genus_species
#   - Standard: Genus_species_TaxID
#   - Full: Genus_species_TaxID_UniprotID_GeneName
# 
# Parsing logic by position:
#   Position 1: Always genus (taxonomic genus)
#   Position 2: Always species (species epithet)
#   Position 3: TaxID (NCBI Taxonomy ID, must be numeric)
#   Position 4: UniProt ID (if valid format) OR first part of protein name
#   Position 5+: Protein/gene name (joined with underscores if multi-word)
# 
# Parameters:
#   labels - character vector of original tip labels from phylogenetic tree
# 
# Returns:
#   data.frame with columns:
#     - original_label:       unchanged input label
#     - genus:               taxonomic genus (first component)
#     - species:             species epithet (second component)
#     - taxid:               NCBI Taxonomy ID (third component, numeric only)
#     - uniprot_id:          UniProt accession (fourth component if valid format)
#     - protein:             gene/protein description (remaining components)
#     - genus_species_only:  "Genus species" format for metadata matching
# 
# Side effects:
#   - Prints extraction statistics to console
#   - Issues warnings for non-numeric TaxIDs
# 
# Example:
#   labels <- c("Aspergillus_niger_5061_A0A1C7NW11_kinase",
#               "Candida_albicans_237561")
#   result <- extract_taxid_from_labels(labels)

extract_taxid_from_labels <- function(labels) {
  
  cat("\n🔍 Extracting taxonomic components from", length(labels), "labels...\n")
  
  # Initialize result data frame with all required columns
  result <- data.frame(
    original_label = labels,
    genus = NA_character_,
    species = NA_character_,
    taxid = NA_character_,
    uniprot_id = NA_character_,
    protein = NA_character_,
    genus_species_only = NA_character_,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Parse each label according to structured format
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  
  for (i in seq_along(labels)) {
    # Split label by underscore delimiter
    parts <- strsplit(labels[i], "_")[[1]]
    
    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # CASE 1: Full format with at least genus, species, and TaxID
    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    if (length(parts) >= 3) {
      
      # COMPONENT 1: Genus (mandatory)
      result$genus[i] <- parts[1]
      
      # COMPONENT 2: Species (mandatory)
      result$species[i] <- parts[2]
      result$genus_species_only[i] <- paste(parts[1], parts[2])
      
      # COMPONENT 3: TaxID (should be numeric)
      # Validate that third component is purely numeric
      if (grepl("^[0-9]+$", parts[3])) {
        result$taxid[i] <- parts[3]
      } else {
        warning(paste("Label", i, "has non-numeric TaxID:", parts[3]))
        next  # Skip to next label
      }
      
      # COMPONENT 4+: UniProt ID and/or Protein Name
      # This section handles variable label structures
      
      if (length(parts) == 3) {
        # Minimum format: Only Genus_species_TaxID
        result$uniprot_id[i] <- NA_character_
        result$protein[i] <- NA_character_
      
      } else if (length(parts) == 4) {
        # Four components: Check if 4th is UniProt ID or protein name
        if (is_valid_uniprot(parts[4])) {
          result$uniprot_id[i] <- parts[4]
          result$protein[i] <- NA_character_
        } else {
          result$uniprot_id[i] <- NA_character_
          result$protein[i] <- parts[4]
        }
      
      } else if (length(parts) >= 5) {
        # Five or more components: 4th is UniProt ID, rest is protein name
        if (is_valid_uniprot(parts[4])) {
          result$uniprot_id[i] <- parts[4]
          # Join remaining parts with underscores for multi-word protein names
          result$protein[i] <- paste(parts[5:length(parts)], collapse = "_")
        } else {
          # 4th component is not valid UniProt, treat all as protein name
          result$uniprot_id[i] <- NA_character_
          result$protein[i] <- paste(parts[4:length(parts)], collapse = "_")
        }
      }
    
    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # CASE 2: Minimal format with only genus and species
    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    } else if (length(parts) == 2) {
      result$genus[i] <- parts[1]
      result$species[i] <- parts[2]
      result$genus_species_only[i] <- paste(parts[1], parts[2])
    
    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # CASE 3: Edge case with only genus
    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    } else if (length(parts) == 1) {
      result$genus[i] <- parts[1]
      result$genus_species_only[i] <- parts[1]
    }
  }
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Generate extraction statistics
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  
  n_with_genus <- sum(!is.na(result$genus))
  n_with_species <- sum(!is.na(result$species))
  n_with_taxid <- sum(!is.na(result$taxid))
  n_with_uniprot <- sum(!is.na(result$uniprot_id))
  n_with_protein <- sum(!is.na(result$protein))
  
  cat("  ✅ Extraction summary:\n")
  cat("     • Genus:", n_with_genus, "/", length(labels), 
      "(", round(n_with_genus/length(labels)*100, 1), "%)\n")
  cat("     • Species:", n_with_species, "/", length(labels),
      "(", round(n_with_species/length(labels)*100, 1), "%)\n")
  cat("     • TaxID:", n_with_taxid, "/", length(labels),
      "(", round(n_with_taxid/length(labels)*100, 1), "%)\n")
  cat("     • 🧬 UniProt ID:", n_with_uniprot, "/", length(labels),
      "(", round(n_with_uniprot/length(labels)*100, 1), "%)\n")
  cat("     • Protein name:", n_with_protein, "/", length(labels),
      "(", round(n_with_protein/length(labels)*100, 1), "%)\n\n")
  
  return(result)
}

#############################################
### FUNCTION: Clean and format tip labels with mapping
#############################################
# Processes tip labels for display while maintaining mapping to original names
# 
# This function creates clean, readable labels suitable for visualization
# while preserving the connection to original identifiers. This is essential
# for:
#   - Metadata matching (links cleaned names to database records)
#   - Duplicate handling (ensures unique tip labels)
#   - Display optimization (removes clutter from labels)
# 
# Processing pipeline:
#   1. Replace underscores with spaces (optional)
#   2. Normalize whitespace (collapse multiple spaces)
#   3. Remove leading/trailing whitespace
#   4. Remove leading numbers (optional)
#   5. Keep only genus and species (optional)
#   6. Add numbers to duplicates for uniqueness (essential)
#   7. Apply length limit (optional)
# 
# Parameters:
#   labels - character vector of original labels from tree
#   params - list of cleaning parameters (from clean_params global variable)
#            Contains boolean flags for each processing step
# 
# Returns:
#   list with two elements:
#     - cleaned: character vector of processed labels ready for display
#     - mapping: data.frame linking original names to cleaned names
#                Columns: original_label, clean_label_base, clean_label_final
#                Essential for metadata matching workflow
# 
# Important notes:
#   - Duplicate numbering happens AFTER base cleaning
#     This preserves the base name for metadata matching
#   - Length limiting happens LAST to avoid affecting matches
# 
# Example:
#   labels <- c("123_Aspergillus_niger_5061", "124_Aspergillus_niger_5062")
#   result <- clean_tip_labels_with_mapping(labels, clean_params)
#   # Result$cleaned: c("Aspergillus niger (1)", "Aspergillus niger (2)")
#   # Result$mapping: Links back to original IDs for metadata matching

clean_tip_labels_with_mapping <- function(labels, params = clean_params) {
  cleaned <- labels
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # STEP 1: Replace underscores with spaces for readability
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  if (params$replace_underscore) {
    cleaned <- str_replace_all(cleaned, "_", " ")
  }
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # STEP 2: Normalize whitespace
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Collapse multiple spaces to single space
  cleaned <- str_replace_all(cleaned, "\\s+", " ")
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # STEP 3: Remove leading and trailing whitespace
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  cleaned <- str_trim(cleaned)
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # STEP 4: Remove leading numbers if specified
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Some FASTA files have numeric prefixes that are not part of the name
  if (params$remove_numbers) {
    cleaned <- str_replace(cleaned, "^\\d+\\s*", "")
  }
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # STEP 5: Keep only genus and species (first two words)
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # This creates standardized binomial nomenclature
  if (params$keep_only_genus_species) {
    cleaned <- sapply(strsplit(cleaned, " "), function(x) {
      if (length(x) >= 2) {
        paste(x[1], x[2])
      } else {
        x[1]  # If only one word, keep it
      }
    })
  }
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # CRITICAL: Create mapping BEFORE adding duplicate numbers
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # This preserves the base name for metadata matching
  # The base name (without numbers) is used to match with metadata database
  mapping <- data.frame(
    original_label = labels,
    clean_label_base = cleaned,  # Without duplicate numbers
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # STEP 6: Add numbers to duplicate names to ensure uniqueness
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Phylogenetic trees cannot have duplicate tip labels
  # This step ensures uniqueness while preserving the base name
  if (params$add_number_to_duplicates) {
    dup_counts <- table(cleaned)
    duplicates <- names(dup_counts[dup_counts > 1])
    
    for (dup in duplicates) {
      indices <- which(cleaned == dup)
      for (j in seq_along(indices)) {
        # Format: "Genus species (1)", "Genus species (2)", etc.
        cleaned[indices[j]] <- paste0(cleaned[indices[j]], " (", j, ")")
      }
    }
  }
  
  # Add final cleaned labels to mapping
  # This is the version that will appear in the tree
  mapping$clean_label_final <- cleaned
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # STEP 7: Apply length limit if specified (optional)
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Useful for extremely long species names
  if (!is.null(params$max_length)) {
    cleaned <- str_trunc(cleaned, width = params$max_length, 
                        side = "right", ellipsis = "...")
    mapping$clean_label_final <- cleaned
  }
  
  cat("✓ Labels cleaned:", length(labels), "taxa\n")
  return(list(cleaned = cleaned, mapping = mapping))
}

#############################################
### FUNCTION: Load metadata from file
#############################################
# Reads metadata file and validates required columns
# 
# The metadata file should contain taxonomic and biological information
# for organisms in the phylogenetic tree. This function performs validation
# and preprocessing to ensure compatibility with downstream analyses.
# 
# Supported file formats:
#   - Tab-separated values (.tsv) - PRIMARY FORMAT
#   - Comma-separated values (.csv) - FALLBACK
# 
# Required columns:
#   - Organism: Species name (must match tree tip labels after cleaning)
#   - TaxIDs: NCBI Taxonomy ID (numeric identifier)
# 
# Optional columns (used if available):
#   - Kingdom: Taxonomic kingdom (e.g., Fungi, Plantae)
#   - Phylum: Taxonomic phylum (e.g., Ascomycota, Basidiomycota)
#   - Early: Early diverging status (Yes/No/Not applicable)
#   - Considered: Ecological category (e.g., "Soil fungus", "Aquatic")
# 
# Parameters:
#   metadata_path - character string with path to metadata file
# 
# Returns:
#   data.frame with metadata
#   Includes new column: Organism_clean (trimmed organism names for matching)
# 
# Stops execution if:
#   - File not found at specified path
#   - Required columns (Organism, TaxIDs) are missing
#   - File cannot be parsed as TSV or CSV
# 
# Side effects:
#   - Prints loading confirmation and column list
#   - Cleans TaxID column (removes non-numeric characters like "taxid:" prefix)
# 
# Example:
#   metadata <- load_metadata("data/Metadata.tsv")

load_metadata <- function(metadata_path) {
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Verify file existence
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  if (!file.exists(metadata_path)) {
    stop(paste("ERROR: Metadata file not found:", metadata_path))
  }
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Attempt to read file (TSV first, then CSV as fallback)
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  metadata <- tryCatch({
    # PRIMARY: Try reading as tab-separated file
    read.table(metadata_path, header = TRUE, sep = "\t", 
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE, quote = "", 
               fill = TRUE, comment.char = "")
  }, error = function(e) {
    # FALLBACK: Try reading as comma-separated file
    tryCatch({
      read.csv(metadata_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    }, error = function(e2) {
      stop(paste("ERROR: Cannot parse metadata file. Error:", e2$message))
    })
  })
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Validate required columns
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  required_cols <- c("Organism", "TaxIDs")
  missing_cols <- required_cols[!required_cols %in% colnames(metadata)]
  
  if (length(missing_cols) > 0) {
    stop(paste("ERROR: Missing required columns:", 
               paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", ")))
  }
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Clean TaxID column
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Some databases include prefixes like "taxid:" or "NCBITaxon:" 
  # These must be removed for matching
  metadata$TaxIDs <- gsub("[^0-9]", "", as.character(metadata$TaxIDs))
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Create cleaned organism name column for matching
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Handles trailing/leading whitespace that could prevent matching
  metadata$Organism_clean <- str_trim(metadata$Organism)
  
  cat("✓ Metadata loaded:", nrow(metadata), "organisms\n")
  cat("  Columns available:", paste(colnames(metadata), collapse = ", "), "\n")
  
  return(metadata)
}

#############################################
### FUNCTION: Match tree tips with metadata
#############################################
# Links tree tip labels with metadata using hierarchical matching strategy
# 
# This function implements a three-tier matching system to maximize
# the number of successful matches between phylogenetic tree tips
# and the metadata database. The hierarchical approach ensures that
# the most reliable matching method is attempted first, with fallbacks
# for cases where primary methods fail.
# 
# Matching Strategy (in order of reliability):
#   1. TaxID extracted from label structure (MOST RELIABLE)
#      - Direct database identifier
#      - Unambiguous matching
#      - Example: "Aspergillus_niger_5061" → TaxID = 5061
# 
#   2. Organism name matching (GOOD RELIABILITY)
#      - Uses cleaned "Genus species" format
#      - Standardized names for consistent matching
#      - Example: "Aspergillus niger" matches metadata
# 
#   3. TaxID from FASTA header prefix (FALLBACK)
#      - Handles legacy FASTA formats
#      - Extracts TaxID from ">12345|..." format
#      - Less common but useful for compatibility
# 
# Parameters:
#   tree_data - data.frame from extract_taxid_from_labels()
#               Contains parsed taxonomic components
#   metadata  - data.frame from load_metadata()
#               Contains organism information and metadata
# 
# Returns:
#   list with two elements:
#     - data: tree_data with added metadata columns
#             (Kingdom, Phylum, Early, Considered, match status)
#     - report: list with matching statistics
#               (total, matched, unmatched, match rates by method)
# 
# Side effects:
#   - None (pure function, no file I/O or printing)
# 
# Example:
#   tree_data <- extract_taxid_from_labels(tree$tip.label)
#   metadata <- load_metadata("data/Metadata.tsv")
#   result <- match_tree_metadata(tree_data, metadata)
#   print_matching_report(result)  # Display results

match_tree_metadata <- function(tree_data, metadata) {
  matched <- tree_data
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Initialize metadata columns with default values
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  matched$metadata_match <- FALSE            # Boolean: was match successful?
  matched$match_method <- NA_character_      # Which method succeeded?
  matched$Kingdom <- NA_character_           # Taxonomic kingdom
  matched$Phylum <- NA_character_            # Taxonomic phylum
  matched$Early <- NA_character_             # Early diverging status
  matched$Considered <- NA_character_        # Ecological category
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Initialize counters for matching statistics
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  match_by_taxid <- 0           # Matches via extracted TaxID
  match_by_name <- 0            # Matches via organism name
  match_by_partial_taxid <- 0  # Matches via FASTA header TaxID
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Attempt matching for each tip in the tree
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(matched))) {
    meta_idx <- integer(0)         # Index in metadata (empty if no match)
    match_method <- NA_character_  # Method that succeeded
    
    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # TIER 1: Match by extracted TaxID (most reliable)
    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    if (!is.na(matched$taxid[i]) && matched$taxid[i] != "") {
      # Clean TaxID (extract only numeric characters)
      # Some labels may have prefixes like "taxid:" that need removal
      clean_taxid <- gsub("[^0-9]", "", matched$taxid[i])
      
      if (nchar(clean_taxid) > 0) {
        # Search for this TaxID in metadata
        meta_idx <- which(metadata$TaxIDs == clean_taxid)
        
        if (length(meta_idx) > 0) {
          match_method <- "TaxID_extracted"
          match_by_taxid <- match_by_taxid + 1
        }
      }
    }
    
    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # TIER 2: Match by organism name (fallback if TaxID match failed)
    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    if (length(meta_idx) == 0 && !is.na(matched$genus_species_only[i])) {
      # Search using standardized "Genus species" format
      meta_idx <- which(metadata$Organism_clean == matched$genus_species_only[i])
      
      if (length(meta_idx) > 0) {
        match_method <- "Organism_name"
        match_by_name <- match_by_name + 1
      }
    }
    
    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # TIER 3: Match by TaxID at start of label (legacy FASTA format)
    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    if (length(meta_idx) == 0) {
      original_label <- matched$original_label[i]
      
      # Extract numbers at beginning after ">" (FASTA header format)
      # Matches patterns like: ">12345|..." or ">12345 ..."
      taxid_match <- stringr::str_match(original_label, "^>?([0-9]+)[|\\s]")
      
      if (!is.na(taxid_match[1, 2])) {
        partial_taxid <- taxid_match[1, 2]
        
        # Search for this TaxID in metadata
        meta_idx <- which(metadata$TaxIDs == partial_taxid)
        
        if (length(meta_idx) > 0) {
          match_method <- "TaxID_partial"
          match_by_partial_taxid <- match_by_partial_taxid + 1
          
          # Update taxid in matched data for future reference
          matched$taxid[i] <- partial_taxid
        }
      }
    }
    
    # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    # Transfer metadata if match was found
    # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    if (length(meta_idx) > 0) {
      matched$metadata_match[i] <- TRUE
      matched$match_method[i] <- match_method
      
      # Transfer Kingdom if column exists in metadata
      if ("Kingdom" %in% colnames(metadata)) {
        matched$Kingdom[i] <- metadata$Kingdom[meta_idx[1]]
      }
      
      # Transfer Phylum if column exists in metadata
      if ("Phylum" %in% colnames(metadata)) {
        matched$Phylum[i] <- metadata$Phylum[meta_idx[1]]
      }
      
      # Transfer Early diverging status if column exists
      if ("Early" %in% colnames(metadata)) {
        matched$Early[i] <- metadata$Early[meta_idx[1]]
      }
      
      # Transfer Ecological Category if column exists
      if ("Considered" %in% colnames(metadata)) {
        matched$Considered[i] <- metadata$Considered[meta_idx[1]]
      }
    }
  }
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Replace NA values with "Unknown" for visualization compatibility
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  matched$Kingdom[is.na(matched$Kingdom)] <- "Unknown"
  matched$Phylum[is.na(matched$Phylum)] <- "Unknown"
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Generate comprehensive matching report
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  report <- list(
    total_tips = nrow(matched),
    matched = sum(matched$metadata_match),
    unmatched = sum(!matched$metadata_match),
    match_rate = round(sum(matched$metadata_match) / nrow(matched) * 100, 1),
    by_taxid = match_by_taxid,
    by_name = match_by_name,
    by_partial_taxid = match_by_partial_taxid
  )
  
  return(list(data = matched, report = report))
}

#############################################
### FUNCTION: Print metadata matching report
#############################################
# Displays detailed diagnostic report of tree-metadata matching success
# 
# This function provides essential quality control information for
# assessing the success of the metadata matching process. The report
# helps identify:
#   - Overall matching success rate
#   - Which matching methods were most effective
#   - Which organisms failed to match (for troubleshooting)
#   - Kingdom distribution of matched organisms
# 
# Parameters:
#   match_result - list from match_tree_metadata()
#                  Contains both matched data and statistics
# 
# Returns:
#   NULL (invisible)
# 
# Side effects:
#   - Prints formatted report to console with:
#     * Overall statistics (total, matched, unmatched, percentage)
#     * Breakdown by matching method
#     * List of unmatched tips (up to 10 examples)
#     * Kingdom distribution of matched organisms
# 
# Example:
#   result <- match_tree_metadata(tree_data, metadata)
#   print_matching_report(result)

print_matching_report <- function(match_result) {
  rep <- match_result$report
  data <- match_result$data
  
  cat("\n╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗\n")
  cat("║         TREE-METADATA MATCHING REPORT (ENHANCED)            ║\n")
  cat("╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝\n\n")
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Overall matching statistics
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  cat("📊 Overall Summary:\n")
  cat("   Total tips in tree:", rep$total_tips, "\n")
  cat("   ✅ Successfully matched:", rep$matched, "(", rep$match_rate, "%)\n")
  cat("   ❌ Failed to match:", rep$unmatched, "\n\n")
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Breakdown by matching method
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  cat("🔍 Matching Method Breakdown:\n")
  cat("   • Tier 1 (Extracted TaxID):", rep$by_taxid, "\n")
  cat("   • Tier 2 (Organism name):", rep$by_name, "\n")
  cat("   • Tier 3 (Partial TaxID from header):", rep$by_partial_taxid, "\n\n")
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Display unmatched tips for troubleshooting
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  if (rep$unmatched > 0) {
    unmatched <- data[!data$metadata_match, ]
    cat("⚠️  Unmatched Tips (showing first 10):\n")
    cat("   These organisms were not found in metadata and need review:\n\n")
    
    for (i in seq_len(min(10, nrow(unmatched)))) {
      cat("   ", i, ". ", unmatched$genus_species_only[i], "\n", sep = "")
      cat("      TaxID: ", 
          ifelse(is.na(unmatched$taxid[i]), "Not extracted", unmatched$taxid[i]), "\n", sep = "")
      cat("      Original label: ", substr(unmatched$original_label[i], 1, 60), "...\n\n", sep = "")
    }
    
    if (nrow(unmatched) > 10) {
      cat("   ... and", nrow(unmatched) - 10, "more unmatched tip(s)\n\n")
    }
    
    cat("   💡 Tip: Check if these organisms exist in your metadata file\n")
    cat("      or if their names/TaxIDs need standardization.\n\n")
  }
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Display Kingdom distribution of matched organisms
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  matched_data <- data[data$metadata_match, ]
  if (nrow(matched_data) > 0 && !all(is.na(matched_data$Kingdom))) {
    cat("🌍 Kingdom Distribution (matched organisms only):\n")
    kingdom_table <- table(matched_data$Kingdom)
    for (kingdom in names(sort(kingdom_table, decreasing = TRUE))) {
      cat("   • ", sprintf("%-15s", kingdom), ": ", kingdom_table[kingdom], "\n", sep = "")
    }
  }
  
  cat("\n═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n")
}

#############################################
### FUNCTION: Generate missing metadata template
#############################################
# Creates a template file for organisms not found in metadata database
# 
# This function facilitates the process of adding new organisms to the
# metadata by generating a pre-formatted template with all required columns.
# Users can fill in the "[TO_FILL]" placeholders and add the data to their
# main metadata file.
# 
# Parameters:
#   match_result - list from match_tree_metadata()
#                  Contains matching results and unmatched organisms
# 
# Returns:
#   data.frame template with missing organisms, or NULL if all matched
# 
# Side effects:
#   - Writes TSV template file to presence_absence_dir
#   - Filename: {gene}_missing_Metadata.tsv
# 
# Template columns:
#   - Organism: Species name (pre-filled from tree)
#   - TaxIDs: NCBI Taxonomy ID (pre-filled if available, otherwise "[TO_FILL]")
#   - Considered, Kingdom, Phylum, Early: "[TO_FILL]" placeholders
#   - Interaction fields: "[TO_FILL]" placeholders
# 
# Example:
#   result <- match_tree_metadata(tree_data, metadata)
#   template <- generate_missing_metadata(result)
#   # User fills in template and adds to main metadata file

generate_missing_metadata <- function(match_result) {
  # Extract organisms that failed to match
  missing <- match_result$data[!match_result$data$metadata_match, ]
  
  if (nrow(missing) == 0) {
    cat("✓ All organisms successfully matched with metadata!\n")
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  cat("📝 Creating metadata template for", nrow(missing), "unmatched organism(s)...\n")
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Create template with missing organisms
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  template <- data.frame(
    Organism = missing$genus_species_only,
    TaxIDs = ifelse(is.na(missing$taxid), "[TO_FILL]", missing$taxid),
    Considered = "[TO_FILL]",
    Kingdom = "[TO_FILL]",
    Phylum = "[TO_FILL]",
    Early = "[TO_FILL]",
    Interaction = "[TO_FILL]",
    OrganismInteracts = "[TO_FILL]",
    TypeInteraction = "[TO_FILL]",
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  # Remove duplicate organisms (same species appearing multiple times)
  template <- template[!duplicated(template$Organism), ]
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Write template to file
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  output_path <- file.path(presence_absence_dir,
                          paste0(file, "_missing_Metadata.tsv"))
  
  write.table(template,
              file = output_path,
              sep = "\t", 
              row.names = FALSE,
              quote = FALSE)
  
  cat("✓ Template saved:", output_path, "\n")
  cat("  Please fill in '[TO_FILL]' values and add to main metadata file.\n")
  
  return(template)
}

#############################################
### FUNCTION: Get tree statistics
#############################################
# Calculates basic phylogenetic tree characteristics
# 
# Provides essential information about tree structure and data availability
# Used for quality control and method selection (e.g., bootstrap display)
# 
# Parameters:
#   tree - phylo object from ape::read.tree()
# 
# Returns:
#   list with tree characteristics:
#     - n_tips: Number of terminal nodes (taxa)
#     - n_nodes: Number of internal nodes
#     - total_length: Sum of all branch lengths
#     - is_rooted: Boolean, whether tree has a root
#     - is_binary: Boolean, whether tree is fully bifurcating
#     - has_bootstrap: Boolean, presence of node labels (bootstrap values)
#     - has_branch_lengths: Boolean, presence of branch length data
# 
# Example:
#   tree <- read.tree("gene.nwk")
#   stats <- get_tree_stats(tree)
#   print_tree_stats(stats)

get_tree_stats <- function(tree) {
  list(
    n_tips = length(tree$tip.label),
    n_nodes = tree$Nnode,
    total_length = sum(tree$edge.length, na.rm = TRUE),
    is_rooted = is.rooted(tree),
    is_binary = is.binary(tree),
    has_bootstrap = !is.null(tree$node.label) && any(!is.na(tree$node.label)),
    has_branch_lengths = !is.null(tree$edge.length) && any(!is.na(tree$edge.length))
  )
}

#############################################
### FUNCTION: Print tree statistics
#############################################
# Displays formatted tree statistics for quality control
# 
# Parameters:
#   stats - list from get_tree_stats()
# 
# Returns:
#   NULL (invisible)
# 
# Side effects:
#   Prints formatted statistics to console

print_tree_stats <- function(stats) {
  cat("\n╔═══════════════════════════════════════╗\n")
  cat("║        TREE STATISTICS                ║\n")
  cat("╚═══════════════════════════════════════╝\n\n")
  
  cat("📊 Tree Structure:\n")
  cat("   Taxa (tips):", stats$n_tips, "\n")
  cat("   Internal nodes:", stats$n_nodes, "\n")
  cat("   Total tree length:", round(stats$total_length, 4), "\n\n")
  
  cat("🔧 Tree Properties:\n")
  cat("   Rooted:", ifelse(stats$is_rooted, "Yes ✓", "No ✗"), "\n")
  cat("   Binary (fully bifurcating):", ifelse(stats$is_binary, "Yes ✓", "No ✗"), "\n\n")
  
  cat("📈 Available Data:\n")
  cat("   Bootstrap values:", ifelse(stats$has_bootstrap, "Yes ✓", "No ✗"), "\n")
  cat("   Branch lengths:", ifelse(stats$has_branch_lengths, "Yes ✓", "No ✗"), "\n\n")
}

#############################################
### FUNCTION: Generate presence/absence table for single gene
#############################################
# Creates a binary table indicating which organisms are present in the tree
# 
# This function generates a comprehensive presence/absence matrix that:
#   - Lists all organisms from metadata
#   - Marks which organisms appear in the phylogenetic tree
#   - Includes UniProt IDs and protein names when available
#   - Adds taxonomic information (TaxID, Kingdom, Phylum, Early status)
#   - Handles organisms found in tree but not in metadata
# 
# Parameters:
#   tree_tips          - character vector of cleaned tip labels from the tree
#   metadata           - data.frame with organism information
#   tree_with_metadata - data.frame with parsed tree data (optional but recommended)
#                        Used to extract UniProt IDs and protein names
#   gene_name          - character string with gene identifier (e.g., "IPT", "LOG")
#   output_file        - character string with path to save TSV file
# 
# Returns:
#   data.frame with presence/absence information
#   Columns: Organism, {gene_name}, UniProt_ID, Protein, TaxIDs, Kingdom, Phylum, Early
# 
# Side effects:
#   - Writes TSV file to disk at output_file path
#   - Prints progress and statistics to console
# 
# Example:
#   tree <- read.tree("LOG.nwk")
#   metadata <- load_metadata("data/Metadata.tsv")
#   tree_data <- extract_taxid_from_labels(tree$tip.label)
#   
#   table <- generate_presence_absence_table(
#     tree_tips = tree$tip.label,
#     metadata = metadata,
#     tree_with_metadata = tree_data,
#     gene_name = "LOG",
#     output_file = "output/LOG_presence.tsv"
#   )

generate_presence_absence_table <- function(tree_tips, 
                                             metadata, 
                                             tree_with_metadata = NULL, 
                                             gene_name, 
                                             output_file) {
  
  cat("\n🔍 Generating presence/absence table for:", gene_name, "\n")
  
  # ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
  # CRITICAL: Clean labels BEFORE comparing
  # Remove [Phy] and numbers (1), (2) for matching
  # ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
  
  clean_for_matching <- function(labels) {
    # Step 1: Remove [Phy] at the end
    labels <- gsub("\\s*\\[[^]]+\\]\\s*$", "", labels)
    # Step 2: Remove (1), (2), etc.
    labels <- gsub("\\s*\\([0-9]+\\)\\s*$", "", labels)
    # Step 3: Trim whitespace
    labels <- trimws(labels)
    return(labels)
  }
  
  # Clean tree tips for matching
  tree_tips_clean <- clean_for_matching(tree_tips)
  
  # STEP 1: Get all organism names from metadata (reference)
  all_organisms <- metadata$Organism_clean
  
  # STEP 2: Identify organisms in tree (using cleaned labels)
  organisms_in_tree_clean <- unique(tree_tips_clean)
  new_organisms <- setdiff(organisms_in_tree_clean, all_organisms)
  
  if (length(new_organisms) > 0) {
    cat("  ⚠️  Found", length(new_organisms), "organisms in tree not present in metadata\n")
    cat("     Adding them to the table...\n")
  }
  
  # STEP 3: Combine all organisms
  complete_organism_list <- c(all_organisms, new_organisms)
  
  # STEP 4: Create presence/absence column
  presence <- complete_organism_list %in% organisms_in_tree_clean
  
  # STEP 5: Build the table
  presence_table <- data.frame(
    Organism = complete_organism_list,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  presence_table[[gene_name]] <- presence
  presence_table$UniProt_ID <- NA_character_
  presence_table$Protein <- NA_character_
  
  # STEP 6: Add metadata columns + UniProt ID + Protein name
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(presence_table))) {
    org <- presence_table$Organism[i]
    
    # ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
    # SEARCH IN tree_with_metadata for UniProt ID
    # ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
    if (!is.null(tree_with_metadata)) {
      # Search using genus_species_only (already clean)
      tree_idx <- which(tree_with_metadata$genus_species_only == org)
      
      if (length(tree_idx) > 0) {
        if ("uniprot_id" %in% colnames(tree_with_metadata)) {
          # Get ALL UniProt IDs for this organism
          uniprot_ids <- tree_with_metadata$uniprot_id[tree_idx]
          # Filter out NAs
          uniprot_ids <- uniprot_ids[!is.na(uniprot_ids) & uniprot_ids != ""]
          # Join with commas if multiple exist
          if (length(uniprot_ids) > 0) {
            presence_table$UniProt_ID[i] <- paste(unique(uniprot_ids), collapse = ", ")
          }
        }
        
        # ✅ ADD PROTEIN NAME
        if ("protein" %in% colnames(tree_with_metadata)) {
          protein_names <- tree_with_metadata$protein[tree_idx]
          protein_names <- protein_names[!is.na(protein_names) & protein_names != ""]
          if (length(protein_names) > 0) {
            presence_table$Protein[i] <- paste(unique(protein_names), collapse = ", ")
          }
        }
      }
    }
    
    # ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
    # Search in metadata for TaxID, Kingdom, etc.
    # ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
    meta_idx <- which(metadata$Organism_clean == org)
    
    if (length(meta_idx) > 0) {
      if ("TaxIDs" %in% colnames(metadata)) {
        presence_table$TaxIDs[i] <- metadata$TaxIDs[meta_idx[1]]
      }
      if ("Kingdom" %in% colnames(metadata)) {
        presence_table$Kingdom[i] <- metadata$Kingdom[meta_idx[1]]
      }
      if ("Phylum" %in% colnames(metadata)) {
        presence_table$Phylum[i] <- metadata$Phylum[meta_idx[1]]
      }
      if ("Early" %in% colnames(metadata)) {
        presence_table$Early[i] <- metadata$Early[meta_idx[1]]
      }
    } else {
      presence_table$TaxIDs[i] <- NA_character_
      presence_table$Kingdom[i] <- "Unknown"
      presence_table$Phylum[i] <- "Unknown"
      presence_table$Early[i] <- NA_character_
    }
  }
  
  # STEP 7: Reorder columns
  column_order <- c("Organism", gene_name)
  
  if ("UniProt_ID" %in% colnames(presence_table)) {
    column_order <- c(column_order, "UniProt_ID")
  }
  if ("Protein" %in% colnames(presence_table)) {
    column_order <- c(column_order, "Protein")
  }
  
  remaining <- setdiff(colnames(presence_table), column_order)
  column_order <- c(column_order, remaining)
  
  presence_table <- presence_table[, column_order]
  
  # STEP 8: Sort
  presence_table <- presence_table[order(-presence_table[[gene_name]], 
                                          presence_table$Organism), ]
  
  # STEP 9: Write to file
  write.table(
    presence_table,
    file = output_file,
    sep = "\t",
    row.names = FALSE,
    quote = FALSE,
    na = ""
  )
  
  # STEP 10: Report
  n_present <- sum(presence_table[[gene_name]])
  n_total <- nrow(presence_table)
  percentage <- round(n_present / n_total * 100, 1)
  
  if ("UniProt_ID" %in% colnames(presence_table)) {
    n_with_uniprot <- sum(!is.na(presence_table$UniProt_ID) & 
                           presence_table$UniProt_ID != "")
    uniprot_pct <- round(n_with_uniprot / n_present * 100, 1)
    
    cat("  ✅ Table created successfully\n")
    cat("     Organisms present:", n_present, "/", n_total, "(", percentage, "%)\n")
    cat("     With UniProt ID:", n_with_uniprot, "/", n_present, 
        "(", uniprot_pct, "% of present)\n")
  } else {
    cat("  ✅ Table created successfully\n")
    cat("     Organisms present:", n_present, "/", n_total, "(", percentage, "%)\n")
  }
  
  cat("     Saved to:", output_file, "\n")
  
  return(presence_table)
}

#############################################
### FUNCTION: Merge individual gene tables into consolidated hormone table
#############################################
# Combines multiple single-gene presence/absence tables into one master table
# 
# This function consolidates data from multiple genes analyzed in the same
# hormone/project category. It's essential for comparative genomics analyses
# where you want to see which organisms have which genes.
# 
# The merging process:
#   1. Reads all individual gene TSV files from a directory
#   2. Starts with organisms from metadata
#   3. Adds organisms found in trees but not in metadata
#   4. Creates binary columns for each gene
#   5. Calculates N_Genes (how many genes each organism has)
#   6. Sorts by gene count (descending)
# 
# Parameters:
#   presence_absence_dir - path to directory containing individual gene tables
#                          Expected files: {gene}.tsv
#   output_file          - path to save the consolidated TSV file
#   metadata             - data.frame with organism information
# 
# Returns:
#   data.frame with consolidated presence/absence information
#   Columns: Organism, TaxIDs, Kingdom, Phylum, Early, {gene1}, {gene2}, ..., N_Genes
# 
# Side effects:
#   - Writes consolidated TSV file to disk
#   - Prints detailed progress and statistics
# 
# Example:
#   metadata <- load_metadata("data/Metadata.tsv")
#   
#   consolidated <- merge_gene_tables(
#     presence_absence_dir = "phylogenetic/CK/09_presence-absence",
#     output_file = "phylogenetic/CK/merged-genes.tsv",
#     metadata = metadata
#   )

merge_gene_tables <- function(presence_absence_dir, output_file, metadata) {
  
  cat("\n📊 Merging gene tables for hormone...\n")
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # STEP 1: Find all individual gene tables
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  gene_files <- list.files(
    presence_absence_dir,
    pattern = "\\.tsv$",
    full.names = TRUE
  )
  
  # Exclude metadata template files
  gene_files <- gene_files[!grepl("_missing_metadata\\.tsv$", gene_files)]
  
  excluded_files <- list.files(
    presence_absence_dir,
    pattern = "_missing_metadata\\.tsv$",
    full.names = FALSE
  )
  
  if (length(gene_files) == 0) {
    cat("  ⚠️  No gene tables found in:", presence_absence_dir, "\n")
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  if (length(excluded_files) > 0) {
    cat("  ℹ️  Excluded metadata template files:", 
        paste(excluded_files, collapse = ", "), "\n")
  }
  
  cat("  Found", length(gene_files), "gene table(s) to merge\n")
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # STEP 2: Initialize merged table with all organisms from metadata
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  all_organisms <- metadata$Organism_clean
  
  merged_table <- data.frame(
    Organism = all_organisms,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  # Add metadata columns
  if ("TaxIDs" %in% colnames(metadata)) {
    merged_table$TaxIDs <- metadata$TaxIDs
  }
  if ("Kingdom" %in% colnames(metadata)) {
    merged_table$Kingdom <- metadata$Kingdom
  }
  if ("Phylum" %in% colnames(metadata)) {
    merged_table$Phylum <- metadata$Phylum
  }
  if ("Early" %in% colnames(metadata)) {
    merged_table$Early <- metadata$Early
  }
  
  # Track organisms found in trees but not in metadata
  all_new_organisms <- character()
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # STEP 3: Read and merge each gene table
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  for (gene_file in gene_files) {
    # Extract gene name from filename (remove .tsv extension)
    gene_name <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(gene_file))
    
    cat("  Processing:", gene_name, "\n")
    
    # Read the gene table
    gene_table <- tryCatch({
      read.table(
        gene_file,
        header = TRUE,
        sep = "\t",
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
        quote = "",
        comment.char = ""
      )
    }, error = function(e) {
      cat("    ⚠️  Error reading file:", e$message, "\n")
      return(NULL)
    })
    
    if (is.null(gene_table)) next
    
    # Identify new organisms (in tree but not in metadata)
    new_organisms <- setdiff(gene_table$Organism, all_organisms)
    
    if (length(new_organisms) > 0) {
      cat("    Adding", length(new_organisms), "new organism(s) from this gene\n")
      all_new_organisms <- unique(c(all_new_organisms, new_organisms))
    }
    
    # Add gene column to merged table
    # Match organisms and transfer presence/absence values
    gene_col_name <- gene_name
    merged_table[[gene_col_name]] <- FALSE  # Initialize with FALSE (absent)
    
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(gene_table))) {
      org <- gene_table$Organism[i]
      presence_value <- gene_table[[gene_name]][i]
      
      # Find matching organism in merged table
      idx <- which(merged_table$Organism == org)
      
      if (length(idx) > 0) {
        # Update presence value
        merged_table[[gene_col_name]][idx[1]] <- presence_value
      }
    }
  }
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # STEP 4: Add new organisms to merged table
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  if (length(all_new_organisms) > 0) {
    cat("\n  📝 Adding", length(all_new_organisms), 
        "organism(s) found in trees but not in metadata\n")
    
    # Create rows for new organisms
    new_rows <- data.frame(
      Organism = all_new_organisms,
      TaxIDs = NA_character_,
      Kingdom = "Unknown",
      Phylum = "Unknown",
      Early = NA_character_,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
    
    # Add gene columns with FALSE values (will be updated below)
    gene_columns <- setdiff(colnames(merged_table), 
                            c("Organism", "TaxIDs", "Kingdom", "Phylum", "Early"))
    
    for (gene_col in gene_columns) {
      new_rows[[gene_col]] <- FALSE
    }
    
    # Re-read gene tables to get presence values for new organisms
    for (gene_file in gene_files) {
      gene_name <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(gene_file))
      gene_table <- read.table(gene_file, header = TRUE, sep = "\t", 
                               stringsAsFactors = FALSE, quote = "", 
                               comment.char = "")
      
      for (i in seq_len(nrow(new_rows))) {
        org <- new_rows$Organism[i]
        gene_idx <- which(gene_table$Organism == org)
        
        if (length(gene_idx) > 0) {
          new_rows[[gene_name]][i] <- gene_table[[gene_name]][gene_idx[1]]
        }
      }
    }
    
    # Append new rows to merged table
    merged_table <- rbind(merged_table, new_rows)
  }
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # STEP 5: Calculate summary statistics per organism
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  gene_columns <- setdiff(colnames(merged_table), 
                          c("Organism", "TaxIDs", "Kingdom", "Phylum", "Early"))
  
  # Count how many genes each organism is present in
  merged_table$N_Genes <- rowSums(merged_table[, gene_columns, drop = FALSE])
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # STEP 6: Sort table by number of genes (descending) and organism name
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  merged_table <- merged_table[order(-merged_table$N_Genes, 
                                      merged_table$Organism), ]
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # STEP 7: Write consolidated table
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  write.table(
    merged_table,
    file = output_file,
    sep = "\t",
    row.names = FALSE,
    quote = FALSE,
    na = ""
  )
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # STEP 8: Generate summary report
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  cat("\n╔═══════════════════════════════════════╗\n")
  cat("║   CONSOLIDATED TABLE SUMMARY          ║\n")
  cat("╚═══════════════════════════════════════╝\n\n")
  
  cat("📊 Table dimensions:\n")
  cat("   Total organisms:", nrow(merged_table), "\n")
  cat("   Total genes:", length(gene_columns), "\n\n")
  
  cat("🧬 Gene coverage (organisms with gene present):\n")
  for (gene_col in gene_columns) {
    n_present <- sum(merged_table[[gene_col]])
    percentage <- round(n_present / nrow(merged_table) * 100, 1)
    cat("   ", sprintf("%-15s", gene_col), ": ", 
        sprintf("%3d", n_present), "/", nrow(merged_table), 
        " (", sprintf("%5.1f", percentage), "%)\n", sep = "")
  }
  
  cat("\n🌍 Organism distribution:\n")
  cat("   From metadata:", sum(merged_table$Kingdom != "Unknown"), "\n")
  cat("   New (not in metadata):", sum(merged_table$Kingdom == "Unknown"), "\n")
  
  cat("\n💾 Output file:\n")
  cat("   Location:", output_file, "\n")
  cat("   Dimensions:", nrow(merged_table), "organisms ×", 
      length(gene_columns), "genes\n")
  cat("═══════════════════════════════════════\n\n")
  
  return(merged_table)
}

#############################################
### FUNCTION: Validate metadata configuration
#############################################
# Performs pre-visualization validation of metadata and visualization parameters
# 
# This function prevents common errors by checking:
#   - Conflicting visualization options (e.g., both branch color AND background)
#   - Required columns exist in metadata
#   - Categorical variables have appropriate number of levels
# 
# Validation categories:
#   1. Kingdom visualization conflicts
#   2. Text visualization conflicts
#   3. Column existence checks
#   4. Early divergence value range
#   5. Strip column availability
# 
# Parameters:
#   tree_data  - data.frame with tree tips and metadata columns
#   viz_params - list with visualization parameters (from viz_params global)
# 
# Returns:
#   list with three elements:
#     - valid: logical, TRUE if no critical errors
#     - messages: character vector of error messages (empty if valid)
#     - warnings: character vector of warning messages (non-critical issues)
# 
# Example:
#   result <- validate_metadata_config(tree_with_metadata, viz_params)
#   if (!result$valid) {
#     print_validation_report(result)
#     stop("Fix validation errors before proceeding")
#   }

validate_metadata_config <- function(tree_data, viz_params) {
  messages <- character(0)
  warnings <- character(0)
  valid <- TRUE
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # VALIDATION 1: Check only one Kingdom option active for branches
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  branch_options <- c(viz_params$kingdom_color_branch, 
                      viz_params$kingdom_background_clade)
  if (sum(branch_options, na.rm = TRUE) > 1) {
    warnings <- c(warnings, 
      "⚠️ WARNING: Both 'kingdom_color_branch' AND 'kingdom_background_clade' are active")
    warnings <- c(warnings,
      "   Recommendation: Use only one. Colored branches OR background highlighting.")
  }
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # VALIDATION 2: Check only one Kingdom option active for text
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  text_options <- c(viz_params$kingdom_color_text, 
                    viz_params$kingdom_background_text)
  if (sum(text_options, na.rm = TRUE) > 1) {
    warnings <- c(warnings,
      "⚠️ WARNING: Both 'kingdom_color_text' AND 'kingdom_background_text' are active")
    warnings <- c(warnings,
      "   Recommendation: Use only one. Colored text OR background highlighting.")
  }
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # VALIDATION 3: Check Kingdom column exists if any Kingdom option is activated
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  if (any(branch_options, text_options, na.rm = TRUE)) {
    if (!viz_params$metadata_kingdom_column %in% colnames(tree_data)) {
      messages <- c(messages,
        paste0("❌ ERROR: Column '", viz_params$metadata_kingdom_column, 
               "' does not exist in metadata"))
      valid <- FALSE
    }
  }
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # VALIDATION 4: Check Early column exists if Early visualization is activated
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  if (viz_params$early_point_shape || viz_params$early_point_fill_color) {
    if (!viz_params$metadata_early_column %in% colnames(tree_data)) {
      messages <- c(messages,
        paste0("❌ ERROR: Column '", viz_params$metadata_early_column,
               "' does not exist in metadata"))
      valid <- FALSE
    }
  }
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # VALIDATION 5: Check strip columns exist if strips are enabled
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  if (viz_params$show_strip_considered) {
    if (!viz_params$strip_considered_column %in% colnames(tree_data)) {
      messages <- c(messages,
        paste0("❌ ERROR: Column '", viz_params$strip_considered_column,
               "' does not exist in metadata"))
      valid <- FALSE
    }
  }
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # VALIDATION 6: Check Early column has reasonable number of values
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  if (viz_params$metadata_early_column %in% colnames(tree_data)) {
    early_values <- unique(tree_data[[viz_params$metadata_early_column]])
    early_values <- early_values[!is.na(early_values)]
    if (length(early_values) > 4) {
      warnings <- c(warnings,
        paste0("⚠️ WARNING: Column '", viz_params$metadata_early_column,
               "' has ", length(early_values), " unique values."))
      warnings <- c(warnings,
        "   Point shapes work best with 3 categories (e.g., Yes/No/Not applicable)")
    }
  }
  
  return(list(
    valid = valid,
    messages = messages,
    warnings = warnings
  ))
}

#############################################
### FUNCTION: Print validation report
#############################################
# Displays validation results in a formatted, user-friendly manner
# 
# Parameters:
#   validation_result - list from validate_metadata_config()
# 
# Returns:
#   NULL (invisible)
# 
# Side effects:
#   Prints formatted report to console with:
#     - Critical errors (prevent execution)
#     - Warnings (non-critical but worth reviewing)
#     - Final validation status

print_validation_report <- function(validation_result) {
  cat("\n╔════════════════════════════════════════════╗\n")
  cat("║   METADATA CONFIGURATION VALIDATION REPORT ║\n")
  cat("╚════════════════════════════════════════════╝\n\n")
  
  # Show errors if any
  if (length(validation_result$messages) > 0) {
    cat("🚨 CRITICAL ERRORS:\n")
    for (msg in validation_result$messages) {
      cat(msg, "\n")
    }
    cat("\n")
  }
  
  # Show warnings if any
  if (length(validation_result$warnings) > 0) {
    cat("⚠️  WARNINGS:\n")
    for (warn in validation_result$warnings) {
      cat(warn, "\n")
    }
    cat("\n")
  }
  
  # Final result
  if (validation_result$valid) {
    if (length(validation_result$warnings) == 0) {
      cat("✅ VALIDATION SUCCESSFUL: No errors or warnings\n")
    } else {
      cat("✅ VALIDATION SUCCESSFUL: No critical errors (warnings present)\n")
    }
  } else {
    cat("❌ VALIDATION FAILED: Fix critical errors before continuing\n")
  }
  cat("\n")
}

#############################################
### FUNCTION: Assign Kingdoms to internal nodes
#############################################
# Propagates Kingdom values from tips to internal nodes based on monophyly
# 
# This function is essential for kingdom_background_clade visualization option.
# It determines which internal nodes should be colored based on whether
# all their descendants belong to the same Kingdom.
# 
# Algorithm:
#   - Uses post-order traversal (process children before parents)
#   - If ALL descendants have same Kingdom → assign that Kingdom
#   - If descendants have mixed Kingdoms → assign "Mixed" (no coloring)
# 
# Parameters:
#   tree        - phylo object from ape::read.tree()
#   kingdom_map - named vector mapping tip labels to Kingdom values
#                 Names: tip labels, Values: Kingdom names
# 
# Returns:
#   data.frame with columns:
#     - node: node number (1:n_tips are tips, rest are internal nodes)
#     - Kingdom: assigned Kingdom value
# 
# Example:
#   tree <- read.tree("gene.nwk")
#   kingdom_map <- setNames(metadata$Kingdom, metadata$Organism_clean)
#   node_kingdoms <- assign_internal_node_kingdoms(tree, kingdom_map)

assign_internal_node_kingdoms <- function(tree, kingdom_map) {

  cat("\n🔄 Analyzing internal nodes for Kingdom assignment...\n")
  
  # Calculate total number of nodes
  n_tips <- length(tree$tip.label)
  n_nodes <- tree$Nnode
  n_total <- n_tips + n_nodes
  
  # Initialize Kingdom vector for ALL nodes
  # Indices 1:n_tips are tips (already have Kingdom from metadata)
  # Indices (n_tips+1):n_total are internal nodes (to be calculated)
  node_kingdoms <- character(n_total)
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # STEP 1: Assign Kingdoms to tips (nodes 1:n_tips)
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  for (i in 1:n_tips) {
    tip_label <- tree$tip.label[i]
    node_kingdoms[i] <- kingdom_map[tip_label]
    if (is.na(node_kingdoms[i])) {
      node_kingdoms[i] <- "Unknown"
    }
  }
  
  cat("  ✓ Tips assigned:", n_tips, "\n")
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # STEP 2: Process internal nodes from leaves to root (post-order)
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # This ensures we process children before parents
  
  internal_nodes <- (n_tips + 1):n_total
  nodes_assigned <- 0
  nodes_mixed <- 0
  
  for (node in internal_nodes) {
    # Get ALL descendants (tips) of this node
    descendants <- phangorn::Descendants(tree, node, type = "tips")[[1]]
    
    if (length(descendants) == 0) {
      # Node without descendants (shouldn't happen in valid tree)
      node_kingdoms[node] <- "Unknown"
      next
    }
    
    # Get Kingdoms of all descendants
    descendant_kingdoms <- node_kingdoms[descendants]
    descendant_kingdoms <- descendant_kingdoms[!is.na(descendant_kingdoms)]
    
    # Check if ALL descendants have the same Kingdom (monophyletic)
    unique_kingdoms <- unique(descendant_kingdoms)
    
    if (length(unique_kingdoms) == 1) {
      # ALL descendants have the same Kingdom → monophyletic clade
      node_kingdoms[node] <- unique_kingdoms[1]
      nodes_assigned <- nodes_assigned + 1
    } else {
      # MIXED - descendants have different Kingdoms → paraphyletic
      node_kingdoms[node] <- "Mixed"
      nodes_mixed <- nodes_mixed + 1
    }
  }
  
  cat("  ✓ Internal nodes processed:", n_nodes, "\n")
  cat("    • Pure nodes (monophyletic):", nodes_assigned, "\n")
  cat("    • Mixed nodes (paraphyletic):", nodes_mixed, "\n")
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Create data.frame with results
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  result <- data.frame(
    node = 1:n_total,
    Kingdom = node_kingdoms,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  return(result)
}

#############################################
### FUNCTION: Generate intelligent Phylum abbreviations
#############################################
# Creates 3-4 letter abbreviations for Phylum names with collision detection
# 
# Abbreviation strategy:
#   - Default: First 3 letters (capitalized first, lowercase rest)
#   - Collisions: Use hardcoded 4-letter abbreviations from lookup table
#   - Format: "Abb" (e.g., "Asco" for Ascomycota)
# 
# Known collisions (hardcoded resolution):
#   - Thermoproteota / Thermotogota → "Thpr" / "Thto"
#   - Chlorophyta / Chloroflexota → "Chlo" / "Chlf"
# 
# Parameters:
#   phyla - character vector of Phylum names
# 
# Returns:
#   list with two elements:
#     - abbreviations: named vector (Names: Phylum, Values: Abbreviation)
#     - legend_table: data.frame with Abbreviation and Phylum columns
#                     Sorted alphabetically by abbreviation
# 
# Example:
#   phyla <- c("Ascomycota", "Basidiomycota", "Chlorophyta")
#   result <- generate_phylum_abbreviations(phyla)
#   # result$abbreviations: c("Ascomycota" = "Asco", "Basidiomycota" = "Bas", ...)

generate_phylum_abbreviations <- function(phyla) {
  
  cat("\n🔤 Generating Phylum abbreviations...\n")
  
  # Remove NAs and empty values
  phyla <- phyla[!is.na(phyla) & phyla != ""]
  phyla_unique <- unique(phyla)
  
  if (length(phyla_unique) == 0) {
    cat("  ⚠️  No Phyla found in data\n")
    return(list(abbreviations = character(0), legend_table = data.frame()))
  }
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # COLLISION RESOLUTION TABLE (hardcoded based on empirical analysis)
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Only the 4 Phyla that collide with 3-letter abbreviations
  
  collision_resolution <- c(
    "Thermoproteota" = "Thpr",
    "Thermotogota" = "Thto",
    "Chlorophyta" = "Chlo",
    "Chloroflexota" = "Chlf"
  )
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # GENERATE ABBREVIATIONS
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  
  abbreviations <- character(length(phyla_unique))
  names(abbreviations) <- phyla_unique
  
  for (phylum in phyla_unique) {
    
    # Check if it's in the collision resolution table
    if (phylum %in% names(collision_resolution)) {
      # Use predefined 4-letter abbreviation
      abbreviations[phylum] <- collision_resolution[phylum]
      
    } else {
      # Use first 3 letters (capitalize first, lowercase rest)
      abb <- substr(phylum, 1, 3)
      # Format: First letter uppercase, rest lowercase
      abbreviations[phylum] <- paste0(
        toupper(substr(abb, 1, 1)),
        tolower(substr(abb, 2, 3))
      )
    }
  }
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # COLLISION VERIFICATION (additional safety check)
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  
  abb_counts <- table(abbreviations)
  collisions <- names(abb_counts[abb_counts > 1])
  
  if (length(collisions) > 0) {
    cat("  ⚠️  WARNING: Unexpected collisions detected:\n")
    for (coll in collisions) {
      affected <- names(abbreviations[abbreviations == coll])
      cat("    •", coll, "→", paste(affected, collapse = ", "), "\n")
    }
    cat("  💡 Please report this to update collision_resolution table\n")
  }
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # CREATE LEGEND TABLE for figure captions
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  
  legend_table <- data.frame(
    Abbreviation = abbreviations,
    Phylum = names(abbreviations),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  # Sort alphabetically by abbreviation for easy lookup
  legend_table <- legend_table[order(legend_table$Abbreviation), ]
  rownames(legend_table) <- NULL
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # STATISTICS REPORT
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  
  n_3letter <- sum(nchar(abbreviations) == 3)
  n_4letter <- sum(nchar(abbreviations) == 4)
  
  cat("  ✓ Abbreviations generated:", length(abbreviations), "Phyla\n")
  cat("    • 3-letter abbreviations:", n_3letter, "\n")
  cat("    • 4-letter abbreviations:", n_4letter, "\n")
  
  # Show 4-letter cases if they exist (collision resolutions)
  if (n_4letter > 0) {
    four_letter <- legend_table[nchar(legend_table$Abbreviation) == 4, ]
    cat("    • 4-letter cases (collision resolution):\n")
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(four_letter))) {
      cat("      -", four_letter$Abbreviation[i], "=", 
          four_letter$Phylum[i], "\n")
    }
  }
  
  return(list(
    abbreviations = abbreviations,
    legend_table = legend_table
  ))
}

#############################################
### FUNCTION: Add Phylum abbreviations to tip labels
#############################################
# Modifies tree tip labels to include [Abb] Phylum annotations
# 
# Label format transformation:
#   Before: "Aspergillus niger"
#   After:  "Aspergillus niger [Asco]"
# 
# This function:
#   1. Generates abbreviations using generate_phylum_abbreviations()
#   2. Creates mapping from tip labels to Phylum
#   3. Appends [Abb] to each tip label
#   4. Stores legend as tree attribute for later export
# 
# Parameters:
#   tree               - phylo object from ape
#   tree_with_metadata - data.frame with metadata and clean_label_final column
#   phylum_column      - name of Phylum column (default "Phylum")
# 
# Returns:
#   phylo object with modified tip.label
#   Attribute added: attr(tree, "phylum_legend") - legend table
# 
# Side effects:
#   - Modifies tree$tip.label in place
#   - Prints progress and statistics
# 
# Example:
#   tree <- read.tree("gene.nwk")
#   tree_with_metadata$clean_label_final <- tree$tip.label
#   tree <- add_phylum_to_labels(tree, tree_with_metadata, "Phylum")

add_phylum_to_labels <- function(tree, tree_with_metadata, 
                                  phylum_column = "Phylum") {
  
  cat("\n🏷️  Adding Phylum abbreviations to tip labels...\n")
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Verify that Phylum column exists
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  if (!phylum_column %in% colnames(tree_with_metadata)) {
    cat("  ⚠️  Column", phylum_column, "not found in metadata\n")
    cat("  Skipping Phylum annotation\n")
    return(tree)
  }
  
  # Get Phyla present in the tree
  phyla_in_tree <- tree_with_metadata[[phylum_column]]
  
  # Generate abbreviation system
  abb_system <- generate_phylum_abbreviations(phyla_in_tree)
  
  if (length(abb_system$abbreviations) == 0) {
    cat("  ⚠️  No Phyla to abbreviate\n")
    return(tree)
  }
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Create mapping: clean_label_final → Phylum abbreviation
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  phylum_map <- setNames(
    tree_with_metadata[[phylum_column]],
    tree_with_metadata$clean_label_final
  )
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Modify tip labels by appending [Abb]
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  new_labels <- tree$tip.label
  tips_annotated <- 0
  tips_no_phylum <- 0
  
  for (i in seq_along(new_labels)) {
    tip_label <- new_labels[i]
    
    # Get Phylum for this tip
    phylum <- phylum_map[tip_label]
    
    if (!is.na(phylum) && phylum != "") {
      # Get abbreviation for this Phylum
      abb <- abb_system$abbreviations[phylum]
      
      if (!is.na(abb)) {
        # Add [Abb] at the end
        new_labels[i] <- paste0(tip_label, " [", abb, "]")
        tips_annotated <- tips_annotated + 1
      }
    } else {
      # No Phylum information available - add empty brackets
      new_labels[i] <- paste0(tip_label, " []")
      tips_no_phylum <- tips_no_phylum + 1
    }
  }
  
  # Update tree with modified labels
  tree$tip.label <- new_labels
  
  cat("  ✓ Labels updated successfully\n")
  cat("    • Tips annotated:", tips_annotated, "\n")
  
  if (tips_no_phylum > 0) {
    cat("    • Tips without Phylum:", tips_no_phylum, "\n")
  }
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Save legend as tree attribute for later export
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  attr(tree, "phylum_legend") <- abb_system$legend_table
  
  cat("\n")
  
  return(tree)
}

#############################################
### FUNCTION: Generate Phylum legend text for figure caption
#############################################
# Creates formatted legend text suitable for scientific publication captions
# 
# Output format:
#   "Phylum abbreviations: Asco = Ascomycota, Bas = Basidiomycota, ..."
# 
# Parameters:
#   tree - phylo object with phylum_legend attribute
#          (created by add_phylum_to_labels)
# 
# Returns:
#   character string with formatted legend text
# 
# Example:
#   tree <- add_phylum_to_labels(tree, metadata)
#   legend_text <- generate_phylum_legend_text(tree)
#   # Use in figure caption or manuscript

generate_phylum_legend_text <- function(tree) {
  
  legend_table <- attr(tree, "phylum_legend")
  
  if (is.null(legend_table) || nrow(legend_table) == 0) {
    return("No Phylum abbreviations used.")
  }
  
  # Format each entry as "Abb = Phylum"
  legend_entries <- paste0(
    legend_table$Abbreviation, 
    " = ", 
    legend_table$Phylum
  )
  
  # Join all entries with commas
  legend_text <- paste(legend_entries, collapse = ", ")
  
  # Add prefix for complete caption text
  full_legend <- paste0(
    "Phylum abbreviations: ",
    legend_text,
    "."
  )
  
  return(full_legend)
}

#############################################
### FUNCTION: Print Phylum legend table to console
#############################################
# Displays formatted legend table for reference and manuscript preparation
# 
# Parameters:
#   tree - phylo object with phylum_legend attribute
# 
# Returns:
#   legend_table (invisible) for programmatic access
# 
# Side effects:
#   - Prints formatted table to console
#   - Shows caption-ready text

print_phylum_legend <- function(tree) {
  
  legend_table <- attr(tree, "phylum_legend")
  
  if (is.null(legend_table) || nrow(legend_table) == 0) {
    cat("No Phylum legend available.\n")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  
  cat("\n╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗\n")
  cat("║              PHYLUM ABBREVIATIONS LEGEND                  ║\n")
  cat("╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝\n\n")
  
  cat("📋 Copy this text to your figure caption:\n")
  cat("───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n")
  cat(generate_phylum_legend_text(tree), "\n")
  cat("───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n")
  
  cat("📊 Full table (", nrow(legend_table), " Phyla):\n\n", sep = "")
  print(legend_table, row.names = FALSE)
  
  cat("\n")
  
  return(invisible(legend_table))
}

#############################################
### FUNCTION: Export Phylum legend to file
#############################################
# Exports Phylum legend in three formats for different use cases
# 
# Generated files:
#   1. TSV format - for import in Excel/R/Python
#   2. TXT format - formatted text for copying to manuscript
#   3. PDF format - visual table for presentations
# 
# Parameters:
#   tree       - phylo object with phylum_legend attribute
#   output_dir - directory path for saving legend files
#   gene_name  - gene identifier for filename prefix
# 
# Returns:
#   list with paths to generated files:
#     - tsv: path to TSV file
#     - txt: path to TXT file
#     - pdf: path to PDF file
# 
# Side effects:
#   - Creates 3 files in output_dir
#   - Prints confirmation messages
# 
# Example:
#   paths <- export_phylum_legend_to_file(tree, "output/figures/LOG", "LOG")
#   # Creates: LOG_phylum_legend.tsv, .txt, .pdf

export_phylum_legend_to_file <- function(tree, output_dir, gene_name) {
  
  # Verify that legend exists
  legend_table <- attr(tree, "phylum_legend")
  
  if (is.null(legend_table) || nrow(legend_table) == 0) {
    cat("⚠️  No Phylum legend to export\n")
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  # ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
  # OPTION 1: TSV File (for import in Excel/R)
  # ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
  legend_file_tsv <- file.path(output_dir, paste0(gene_name, "_phylum_legend.tsv"))
  
  write.table(
    legend_table,
    file = legend_file_tsv,
    sep = "\t",
    row.names = FALSE,
    quote = FALSE
  )
  
  cat("✅ Phylum legend (TSV) exported to:", legend_file_tsv, "\n")
  
  # ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
  # OPTION 2: Formatted text file (for copying to paper)
  # ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
  legend_file_txt <- file.path(output_dir, paste0(gene_name, "_phylum_legend.txt"))
  
  # Generate formatted text
  legend_text <- generate_phylum_legend_text(tree)
  
  # Write to file
  writeLines(
    c(
      "═════════════════════════════════════════════════════",
      "PHYLUM ABBREVIATIONS LEGEND",
      "═════════════════════════════════════════════════════",
      "",
      "For figure caption:",
      "─────────────────────────────────────────────────────",
      legend_text,
      "─────────────────────────────────────────────────────",
      "",
      paste("Full table (", nrow(legend_table), " Phyla):", sep = ""),
      "",
      paste(
        sprintf("%-6s = %s", legend_table$Abbreviation, legend_table$Phylum),
        collapse = "\n"
      ),
      "",
      "═════════════════════════════════════════════════════"
    ),
    legend_file_txt
  )
  
  cat("✅ Phylum legend (TXT) exported to:", legend_file_txt, "\n")
  
  # ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
  # OPTION 3: Create visual graphic of the legend
  # ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
  legend_file_pdf <- file.path(output_dir, paste0(gene_name, "_phylum_legend.pdf"))
  
  # Create visual table with ggplot2
  library(ggplot2)
  library(gridExtra)
  
  # Prepare data for visual table
  legend_table$Index <- seq_len(nrow(legend_table))
  
  # Create plot with table
  p_legend <- ggplot() + 
    theme_void() +
    annotation_custom(
      tableGrob(
        legend_table[, c("Abbreviation", "Phylum")],
        rows = NULL,
        theme = ttheme_default(
          base_size = 10,
          padding = unit(c(4, 4), "mm"),
          core = list(
            fg_params = list(hjust = 0, x = 0.1)
          ),
          colhead = list(
            fg_params = list(fontface = "bold")
          )
        )
      )
    )
  
  # Export PDF
  ggsave(
    filename = legend_file_pdf,
    plot = p_legend,
    width = 6,
    height = max(4, nrow(legend_table) * 0.3),
    units = "in"
  )
  
  cat("✅ Phylum legend (PDF) exported to:", legend_file_pdf, "\n\n")
  
  # Return paths of generated files
  return(list(
    tsv = legend_file_tsv,
    txt = legend_file_txt,
    pdf = legend_file_pdf
  ))
}
```
