# 5. Read and Validate Tree

```{r read_tree}
#############################################
### TREE FILE VALIDATION AND READING
#############################################
# This section performs initial tree file processing:
#   1. Validates file existence and Newick format
#   2. Reads phylogenetic tree structure
#   3. Calculates basic tree statistics
#   4. Previews tip labels for quality control

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# STEP 1: Validate file existence and format
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
validate_file(input_file)

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# STEP 2: Read Newick formatted tree
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# The ape::read.tree() function handles standard Newick format from:
#   - Phylogenetic inference software: IQ-TREE, RAxML, PhyML, FastTree
#   - Analysis software: MEGA, PAUP, FigTree
#   - Online repositories: TreeBASE, NCBI Taxonomy
#
# Newick format specifications:
#   - Branch lengths: numbers after colon (e.g., :0.123)
#   - Bootstrap values: numbers at internal nodes
#   - Tip labels: organism/sequence identifiers
#   - Tree structure: nested parentheses for hierarchical relationships

tree <- tryCatch({
  read.tree(input_file)
}, error = function(e) {
  stop(paste("ERROR reading tree file:", e$message,
             "\n  Check that file is valid Newick format"))
})

cat("✓ Tree file successfully read\n")

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# STEP 3: Calculate and display tree statistics
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# These statistics help assess tree quality and guide visualization choices
tree_stats <- get_tree_stats(tree)
print_tree_stats(tree_stats)

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# STEP 4: Preview tip labels for quality control
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# This helps verify label format before parsing
cat("\n📋 Preview of tip labels (first 5):\n")
print(head(tree$tip.label, 5))
cat("\n")
```

```{r metadata_processing}
#############################################
### METADATA INTEGRATION WORKFLOW
#############################################
# This section integrates metadata with phylogenetic tree data:
#   1. Extracts taxonomic information from tree labels
#   2. Loads metadata from external file
#   3. Matches tree tips with metadata using multiple strategies
#   4. Generates templates for missing organisms
#   5. Creates unified dataset for visualization

#############################################
cat("\n📋 Extracting taxonomic information from tree labels...\n")

### STEP 2: Load and Match Metadata
#############################################
# Metadata provides additional biological context:
#   - Taxonomic classification (Kingdom, Phylum)
#   - Evolutionary status (Early diverging organisms)
#   - Ecological categories (Habitat, lifestyle)

if (viz_params$use_metadata && file.exists(metadata_file)) {

  match_result <- match_tree_metadata(tree_taxid_data, metadata)

  print_matching_report(match_result)

  missing_template <- generate_missing_metadata(match_result)
  
  # Optional: Automatically save missing metadata template
  # Uncomment these lines to enable automatic template generation:
  # if (!is.null(missing_template)) {
  #   write.table(missing_template, 
  #               file = file.path(presence_absence_dir, 
  #                               paste0(file, "_missing_Metadata.tsv")),
  #               sep = "\t", row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)
  #   cat("📝 Missing organisms template saved\n")
  #   cat("   Fill in the information and add to your metadata file.\n")
  # }
  
  # Store matched data for downstream visualization
  tree_with_metadata <- match_result$data
  
} else {
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Handle cases where metadata is unavailable or disabled
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  if (viz_params$use_metadata && !file.exists(metadata_file)) {
    cat("\n⚠️  Warning: Metadata file not found:", metadata_file, "\n")
    cat("   Proceeding without metadata visualization.\n")
    cat("   Tree will be created with basic styling only.\n\n")
  } else {
    cat("\nℹ️  Metadata visualization disabled in parameters.\n")
    cat("   To enable: Set use_metadata = TRUE in viz_params\n\n")
  }
  
  # Disable metadata features and use basic tree data
  viz_params$use_metadata <- FALSE
  tree_with_metadata <- tree_taxid_data
}
```

# 7. Name Cleaning with Mapping

```{r clean_names}
#############################################
### TIP LABEL CLEANING AND MAPPING
#############################################
# This section prepares tip labels for visualization while maintaining
# traceability to original identifiers. This is critical for:
#   - Metadata matching (links cleaned names to database records)
#   - Duplicate handling (ensures unique labels)
#   - Visual clarity (removes technical artifacts)

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# STEP 1: Store original labels for reference
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
original_labels <- tree$tip.label

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# STEP 2: Clean names AND create bidirectional mapping
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# CRITICAL: The mapping preserves connections between:
#   - Original labels (for file tracking)
#   - Base cleaned labels (for metadata matching)
#   - Final cleaned labels (for visualization)

clean_result <- clean_tip_labels_with_mapping(tree$tip.label, clean_params)
tree$tip.label <- clean_result$cleaned
name_mapping <- clean_result$mapping

# Display cleaning results for quality control
cat("\n╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗\n")
cat("║           NAME CLEANING COMPARISON                        ║\n")
cat("╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝\n\n")

comparison <- data.frame(
  Original = head(original_labels, 5),
  Cleaned = head(tree$tip.label, 5)
)
print(comparison)
cat("\n")

#############################################
### STEP 3: Merge Metadata with Cleaned Names
#############################################
# CRITICAL STEP: This links metadata (matched to original names)
# with cleaned names (used in tree visualization)

if (viz_params$use_metadata && exists("match_result")) {
  
  cat("🔗 Linking metadata with cleaned names...\n")
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # CRITICAL FIX: Extract data from match_result correctly
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  
  # Get the matched metadata (THIS IS THE KEY FIX!)
  tree_with_metadata_full <- match_result$data  # ✅ NOT match_result itself!
  
  cat("✓ Extracted metadata from match_result$data\n")
  cat("   Columns:", paste(colnames(tree_with_metadata_full), collapse=", "), "\n\n")
  
  # Verify Kingdom exists
  if (!"Kingdom" %in% colnames(tree_with_metadata_full)) {
    stop("❌ CRITICAL ERROR: Kingdom column missing from match_result$data!\n",
         "   Check your match_metadata_to_tree function.\n")
  }
  
  cat("✓ Kingdom column confirmed present\n")
  cat("   Sample Kingdoms:", paste(head(tree_with_metadata_full$Kingdom, 5), collapse=", "), "\n\n")
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Merge with name_mapping to add clean_label_final
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  
  metadata_with_clean_names <- merge(
    tree_with_metadata_full,  # Has: original_label, Kingdom, Phylum, Early, etc.
    name_mapping,              # Has: original_label, clean_label_final
    by = "original_label",
    all.x = TRUE
  )
  
  cat("✓ Metadata successfully merged with cleaned names\n")
  cat("\n📊 Verificando columnas después del merge:\n")
  cat("   Columnas:", paste(colnames(metadata_with_clean_names), collapse=", "), "\n\n")
  
  # Verify critical columns exist
  required_cols <- c("clean_label_final", "Kingdom", "Phylum", "Early")
  missing_cols <- setdiff(required_cols, colnames(metadata_with_clean_names))
  
  if (length(missing_cols) > 0) {
    stop("❌ CRITICAL ERROR: Missing columns after merge: ", 
         paste(missing_cols, collapse=", "), "\n",
         "   Check the merge operation.\n")
  }
  
  cat("✓ All required columns present\n")
  cat("\n📊 Sample of final integrated data:\n")
  sample_data <- head(metadata_with_clean_names[, c("original_label", "clean_label_final", "Kingdom", "Phylum", "Early")], 5)
  print(sample_data)
  cat("\n")
  
  # Update tree_with_metadata with merged data
  tree_with_metadata <- metadata_with_clean_names
  
  cat("✓ tree_with_metadata updated successfully\n")
  cat("   Total rows:", nrow(tree_with_metadata), "\n")
  cat("   Has Kingdom:", "Kingdom" %in% colnames(tree_with_metadata), "\n\n")
  
} else {
  if (!exists("match_result")) {
    stop("❌ CRITICAL ERROR: match_result does not exist!\n",
         "   Make sure match_metadata_to_tree() was called successfully.\n")
  }
}

#############################################
### STEP 4: Add Phylum Annotations to Tip Labels (Optional)
#############################################
if (viz_params$show_phylum_labels && 
    viz_params$use_metadata && 
    exists("tree_with_metadata")) {
  
  cat("\n🧬 Adding Phylum annotations to tip labels...\n")
  
  # IMPORTANT: This modifies tree$tip.label
  tree <- add_phylum_to_labels(
    tree = tree,
    tree_with_metadata = tree_with_metadata,
    phylum_column = viz_params$metadata_phylum_column
  )
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # CRITICAL FIX: Update clean_label_final to match new tip labels
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  
  # Create mapping from old clean_label_final to new tip labels
  old_labels <- tree_with_metadata$clean_label_final
  
  # The new labels are in the same order as tree$tip.label
  # We need to map based on the ORIGINAL matching
  for (i in 1:nrow(tree_with_metadata)) {
    orig_label <- tree_with_metadata$original_label[i]
    
    # Find position in name_mapping
    map_idx <- which(name_mapping$original_label == orig_label)
    
    if (length(map_idx) > 0) {
      # Get the position in tree
      tree_idx <- which(original_labels == orig_label)
      
      if (length(tree_idx) > 0) {
        # Update with the NEW label (with Phylum suffix)
        tree_with_metadata$clean_label_final[i] <- tree$tip.label[tree_idx[1]]
      }
    }
  }
  
  cat("✓ Phylum annotations successfully added to tree\n")
  cat("✓ clean_label_final updated to match new labels\n\n")
  
  # Verify synchronization
  cat("📊 Verificando sincronización:\n")
  cat("   Primeros 5 tree$tip.label:\n")
  print(head(tree$tip.label, 5))
  cat("\n   Primeros 5 tree_with_metadata$clean_label_final:\n")
  print(head(tree_with_metadata$clean_label_final, 5))
  cat("\n")
  
  # Print legend for reference
  print_phylum_legend(tree)
  
} else {
  # No Phylum labels - just copy the clean labels
  if (viz_params$use_metadata && exists("tree_with_metadata")) {
    cat("\n📋 No Phylum labels requested\n")
    cat("   Ensuring clean_label_final matches tree$tip.label...\n")
    
    # Update clean_label_final to match current tree labels
    for (i in 1:nrow(tree_with_metadata)) {
      orig_label <- tree_with_metadata$original_label[i]
      tree_idx <- which(original_labels == orig_label)
      
      if (length(tree_idx) > 0) {
        tree_with_metadata$clean_label_final[i] <- tree$tip.label[tree_idx[1]]
      }
    }
    
    cat("✓ Synchronization complete\n\n")
  }
}

# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# CONFIGURATION VALIDATION
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Validate metadata configuration before proceeding to visualization
# This prevents common errors and provides actionable feedback

if (viz_params$use_metadata && exists("tree_with_metadata")) {
  cat("\n🔍 Validating metadata visualization configuration...\n")
  validation_result <- validate_metadata_config(tree_with_metadata, viz_params)
  print_validation_report(validation_result)
  
  # Stop execution if critical errors are found
  # This prevents generating incorrect or misleading visualizations
  if (!validation_result$valid) {
    stop("❌ Invalid configuration detected. Please review errors above and fix before proceeding.")
  }
}
```

# 8. Phylogenetic Tree Visualization

```{r create_tree, fig.width=14, fig.height=14}
#############################################
### PHYLOGENETIC TREE VISUALIZATION
#############################################
# This chunk creates publication-quality phylogenetic trees with:
#   - Multiple layout options (circular, rectangular, fan, radial)
#   - Metadata integration (Kingdom, Phylum, Early diverging)
#   - Visual enhancements (bootstrap, branch lengths, lateral strips)
#   - Customizable styling (colors, fonts, sizes)
#
# Total visualization layers: 12 STEPS
# Expected output: High-resolution tree figure ready for publication

#############################################
### STEP 1: Initialize Base Tree Structure
#############################################
# Creates the foundational ggtree object that will be enhanced in subsequent steps
#
# This step establishes:
#   - Tree topology (from phylo object)
#   - Layout type (circular, rectangular, fan, radial)
#   - Branch length display mode (cladogram vs phylogram)
#   - Initial branch styling (color, thickness)
#   - Plot theme and margins
#   - Legend configuration

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Create base ggtree object with conditional branch coloring
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

if (viz_params$use_metadata && viz_params$kingdom_color_branch) {
  # Metadata mode: Branch colors will be applied by Kingdom in STEP 2
  # Don't specify color parameter here
  p <- ggtree(
    tree, 
    layout = viz_params$layout,               # circular, rectangular, fan, radial
    branch.length = viz_params$branch_length_mode,  # "none" or "branch.length"
    size = viz_params$branch_size             # branch thickness
  )
  cat("✓ Base tree created (branches will be colored by Kingdom)\n")
} else {
  # Simple mode: Fixed branch color throughout tree
  p <- ggtree(
    tree, 
    layout = viz_params$layout,
    branch.length = viz_params$branch_length_mode,
    size = viz_params$branch_size,
    color = viz_params$branch_color           # fixed color for all branches
  )
  cat("✓ Base tree created (branches with fixed color)\n")
}

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Add tree geometry and apply base theme
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
p <- p + geom_tree() + theme_tree2()

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Configure hollow center for circular/radial layouts (donut effect)
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
if (viz_params$add_center_circle && viz_params$layout == "circular") {
  # xlim(center_size, NA) creates empty space in the center
  # This creates the characteristic "donut" appearance
  p <- p + xlim(viz_params$center_circle_size, NA)
  cat("✓ Center circle added (donut effect)\n")
}

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Configure legend display based on active metadata visualizations
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# Determine if legend should be shown
# Legend is needed if any of these metadata visualizations are active:
#   - Kingdom-colored branches
#   - Kingdom-colored text
#   - Early diverging shape markers
#   - Early diverging color coding
show_legend <- viz_params$use_metadata && 
               viz_params$show_metadata_legend && 
               (viz_params$kingdom_color_branch || 
                viz_params$kingdom_color_text || 
                viz_params$early_point_shape || 
                viz_params$early_point_fill_color)

if (show_legend) {
  # Legend enabled: Position on right side with professional styling
  p <- p + theme(
    plot.margin = margin(10, 10, 10, 10),
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.justification = c(0, 0.5),
    legend.box = "vertical",
    legend.box.spacing = unit(0.5, "lines"),
    legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = "gray80", linewidth = 0.5),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 9),
    legend.key = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    legend.key.size = unit(0.8, "lines"),
    legend.spacing.y = unit(0.3, "lines"),
    legend.margin = margin(5, 5, 5, 5)
  )
  cat("✓ Legend enabled (metadata visualizations active)\n")
} else {
  # Legend disabled: Hide to maximize tree display area
  p <- p + theme(
    plot.margin = margin(10, 10, 10, 10),
    legend.position = "none"
  )
  cat("ℹ️  Legend disabled (no metadata visualizations active)\n")
}

cat("\n✓ Base tree initialized successfully\n")
cat("  Layout:", viz_params$layout, "\n")
cat("  Mode:", ifelse(viz_params$branch_length_mode == "none", "cladogram", "phylogram"), "\n")
cat("  Tips:", length(tree$tip.label), "\n")
cat("  Nodes:", tree$Nnode, "\n\n")

#############################################
### STEP 2: Apply Kingdom-based Configuration
#############################################
# Integrates taxonomic Kingdom information into the tree visualization
#
# This step enables multiple Kingdom-based styling options:
#   OPTION 1: Recursive branch coloring (colors extend to internal nodes)
#   OPTION 2: Clade background highlighting (commented out by default)
#   OPTION 3: Text color by Kingdom
#   OPTION 4: Text background highlighting by Kingdom
#
# All options use the Kingdom column from metadata and respect
# the color palette defined in viz_params$kingdom_colors
if (viz_params$use_metadata && 
    viz_params$metadata_kingdom_column %in% colnames(tree_with_metadata)) {
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # CRITICAL: Create Kingdom mapping ONCE at the beginning
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  kingdom_map <- setNames(
    tree_with_metadata[[viz_params$metadata_kingdom_column]],
    tree_with_metadata$clean_label_final
  )
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # STEP 2.1: Preserve original Kingdom mapping in p$data
  # This MUST be done BEFORE any recursive calculations
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  if (!"Kingdom" %in% colnames(p$data)) {
    p$data$Kingdom <- kingdom_map[p$data$label]
    cat("✓ Original Kingdom mapping added to p$data\n")
  }
  
  # ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # OPTION 1: Branch color by Kingdom (RECURSIVE - extended to internal nodes)
  # ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  if (viz_params$kingdom_color_branch) {
    
    cat("\n🎨 Applying RECURSIVE branch coloring by Kingdom...\n")
    cat("   Branches will be colored until reaching mixed nodes\n\n")
    
    # Verify phangorn availability
    has_phangorn <- requireNamespace("phangorn", quietly = TRUE)
    
    if (!has_phangorn) {
      stop("❌ ERROR: Package 'phangorn' is required for recursive branch coloring.\n",
           "Install with: install.packages('phangorn')\n",
           "Then reload the script.")
    }
    
    # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    # Calculate Kingdoms for internal nodes (ONCE)
    # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    node_kingdom_data <- assign_internal_node_kingdoms(tree, kingdom_map)
    
    # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    # RENAME: Use Kingdom_recursive for branch coloring
    # This does NOT affect the original Kingdom column used by strips
    # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    colnames(node_kingdom_data)[colnames(node_kingdom_data) == "Kingdom"] <- "Kingdom_recursive"
    
    # Add recursive Kingdoms to plot data
    p$data <- dplyr::left_join(
      p$data,
      node_kingdom_data,
      by = "node"
    )
    
    # Apply coloring
    p <- p + 
      geom_tree(
        aes(color = Kingdom_recursive), 
        size = viz_params$branch_size
      ) +
      scale_color_manual(
        values = c(
          viz_params$kingdom_colors,
          "Mixed" = viz_params$branch_color,
          "Unknown" = "#000000"
        ),
        name = "Kingdom",
        na.value = "black",
        breaks = names(viz_params$kingdom_colors)
      )
    
    cat("✓ Recursive branch coloring applied\n")
    cat("  • Branches colored up to first mixed node\n")
    cat("  • Pure clades fully colored toward center\n\n")
  }
  
  # ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # OPTION 2: Clade background by Kingdom
  # ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  if (viz_params$kingdom_background_clade) {
    # Note: This function requires kingdoms to be monophyletic
    # If mixed, it will look chaotic

    # Get ancestral nodes for each Kingdom
    kingdoms <- unique(kingdom_map)
    kingdoms <- kingdoms[!is.na(kingdoms)]

    for (k in kingdoms) {
      # Get tips for this Kingdom
      tips_kingdom <- names(kingdom_map)[kingdom_map == k & !is.na(kingdom_map)]

      # Find most recent common ancestor (MRCA)
      if (length(tips_kingdom) > 1) {
        # Get tip indices in tree
        tip_indices <- which(tree$tip.label %in% tips_kingdom)

        if (length(tip_indices) > 1) {
          mrca_node <- getMRCA(tree, tip_indices)

          if (!is.null(mrca_node)) {
            p <- p +
              geom_hilight(
                node = mrca_node,
                fill = viz_params$kingdom_colors[k],
                alpha = 0.3,
                extend = 0.01
              )
          }
        }
      }
    }
    cat("✓ Clade background applied by Kingdom\n")
    cat("  ⚠️ If kingdoms are mixed, background may appear fragmented\n")
  }
  
  # # ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # # OPTION 2: Clade background by Kingdom (individual tip highlighting)
  # # ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # if (viz_params$kingdom_background_clade) {
  #   
  #   cat("⚠️  Using INDIVIDUAL tip highlighting (not monophyletic clades)\n")
  #   cat("   This works for paraphyletic/polyphyletic groups\n")
  #   
  #   # Get all unique Kingdoms
  #   kingdoms <- unique(kingdom_map)
  #   kingdoms <- kingdoms[!is.na(kingdoms)]
  #   
  #   # For each Kingdom, highlight ALL its tips individually
  #   for (k in kingdoms) {
  #     # Get tips for this Kingdom
  #     tips_kingdom <- names(kingdom_map)[kingdom_map == k & !is.na(kingdom_map)]
  #     
  #     if (length(tips_kingdom) > 0) {
  #       # Get tip indices in tree
  #       tip_indices <- which(tree$tip.label %in% tips_kingdom)
  #       
  #       # KEY: Highlight each tip INDIVIDUALLY, don't search for MRCA
  #       # This works for non-monophyletic groups
  #       for (tip_idx in tip_indices) {
  #         # Get terminal node (leaf node)
  #         # In phylo object, tips are nodes 1:Ntip
  #         leaf_node <- tip_idx
  #         
  #         p <- p + 
  #           geom_hilight(
  #             node = leaf_node,
  #             fill = viz_params$kingdom_colors[k],
  #             extend = 1.0,           # KEY: Extend % toward center
  #             to.bottom = TRUE        # KEY: Allow extension toward circular center
  #           )
  #       }
  #       
  #       cat("  ✓", k, ":", length(tip_indices), "tips highlighted\n")
  #     }
  #   }
  #   
  #   cat("✓ Individual tip backgrounds applied by Kingdom\n")
  #   cat("  Note: Each organism painted separately (works for mixed clades)\n")
  # }
}

# # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# # VERIFICATION: Kingdom Assignment
# # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# if (viz_params$kingdom_color_branch && exists("node_kingdom_data")) {
#   cat("\n🔍 VERIFICATION: Kingdom Assignment\n")
#   cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
#   
#   cat("\n📊 Kingdom distribution (original):\n")
#   kingdom_counts <- table(p$data$Kingdom, useNA = "always")
#   print(kingdom_counts)
#   
#   cat("\n📊 Kingdom_recursive distribution:\n")
#   recursive_counts <- table(p$data$Kingdom_recursive, useNA = "always")
#   print(recursive_counts)
#   
#   cat("\n📊 Internal nodes by Kingdom_recursive:\n")
#   internal_kingdoms <- p$data %>%
#     filter(!isTip) %>%
#     count(Kingdom_recursive)
#   print(internal_kingdoms)
#   
#   cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n")
# }

#############################################
### STEP 3: Add Internal Node Points
#############################################

# Add circular markers at each bifurcation point
# These provide visual anchor points for noof labels (bootstrap)
p <- p + geom_nodepoint(
  aes(subset = !isTip),
  size = viz_params$node_point_size,
  color = "black",
  fill = viz_params$node_point_color,
  shape = 21,
  alpha = 1.0
)

cat("✓ Internal node points added\n")

#############################################
### STEP 4: Add Bootstrap Support Values
#############################################

if (tree_stats$has_bootstrap) {
  # Extract UFBoot values from IQ-TREE format (SH-aLRT/UFBoot)
  # Example: "99.5/100" → extract "100" (UFBoot)
  p$data$bootstrap_value <- sapply(p$data$label, function(x) {
    if (is.na(x) || x == "") return(NA)
    
    if (grepl("/", x)) {
      # Split on "/" and take second value
      parts <- strsplit(as.character(x), "/")[[1]]
      if (length(parts) >= 2) return(as.numeric(parts[2]))
    }
    
    # No "/" found, try direct conversion
    return(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(x)))
  })
  
  # Calculate text rotation for circular layout
  # Flip text 180° on left side (90°-270°) to keep readable
  p$data$bootstrap_angle <- sapply(p$data$angle, function(a) {
    if (is.na(a)) return(0)
    a <- a %% 360
    if (a > 90 && a < 270) return(a + 180)
    return(a)
  })
  
  # Add bootstrap text to nodes
  p <- p + geom_text2(
    aes(
      label = bootstrap_value,
      subset = !isTip & !is.na(bootstrap_value) & 
               bootstrap_value > viz_params$bootstrap_threshold,
      angle = if(viz_params$rotate_branch_text && viz_params$layout == "circular") 
                bootstrap_angle else 0
    ),
    size = viz_params$bootstrap_size,
    color = viz_params$bootstrap_color,
    vjust = 1.3,
    hjust = 0.5,
    fontface = "bold",  
    nudge_x = viz_params$bootstrap_nudge_x  # 0 = automatic positioning
  )
  
  cat("✓ Bootstrap values added (UFBoot threshold >", 
      viz_params$bootstrap_threshold, ")\n")
}

#############################################
### STEP 5: Add Branch Length Values
#############################################

if (tree_stats$has_branch_lengths && viz_params$show_branch_length) {
  # Calculate text rotation for circular layout
  p$data$branch_length_angle <- sapply(p$data$angle, function(a) {
    if (is.na(a)) return(0)
    a <- a %% 360
    if (a > 90 && a < 270) return(a + 180)
    return(a)
  })
  
  # Add branch length text at midpoint of each branch
  p <- p + geom_text2(
    aes(
      label = sprintf("%.3f", branch.length),
      x = branch,  # Position at branch midpoint
      subset = !is.na(branch.length) & 
               branch.length > viz_params$branch_length_threshold,
      angle = if(viz_params$rotate_branch_text && viz_params$layout == "circular") 
                branch_length_angle else 0
    ),
    size = viz_params$branch_length_size,
    color = viz_params$branch_length_color,
    vjust = -0.5,
    hjust = 0.5,
    fontface = "italic"  # Traditional: italic for measurements
  )
  
  cat("✓ Branch lengths added\n")
}

#############################################
### STEP 6: Add points at tips with Early diverging configuration
#############################################
# Applies shape and fill color based on Early metadata
if (viz_params$use_metadata && 
    viz_params$metadata_early_column %in% colnames(tree_with_metadata)) {
  
  # Create mapping from labels to Early
  early_map <- setNames(
    tree_with_metadata[[viz_params$metadata_early_column]],
    tree_with_metadata$clean_label_final
  )
  
  # Add Early to plot data
  p$data$Early <- early_map[p$data$label]
  
  # Apply SHAPE and COLOR (without multiple layers, alpha = 1.0)
  if (viz_params$early_point_shape && viz_params$early_point_fill_color) {
    p <- p + 
      geom_tippoint(
        aes(shape = Early, fill = Early),
        size = viz_params$tip_point_size,
        color = "black",
        alpha = 1.0  # Sin transparencia
      ) +
      scale_shape_manual(
        values = viz_params$early_shapes,
        name = "Early Diverging"
      ) +
      scale_fill_manual(
        values = viz_params$early_colors,
        name = "Early Diverging"
      )
    cat("✅ Tip points with shape AND color by Early (alpha=1.0)\n")
    
  } else if (viz_params$early_point_shape) {
    p <- p + 
      geom_tippoint(
        aes(shape = Early),
        size = viz_params$tip_point_size,
        color = "black",
        fill = viz_params$tip_point_color,
        alpha = 1.0
      ) +
      scale_shape_manual(
        values = viz_params$early_shapes,
        name = "Early Diverging"
      )
    cat("✅ Tip points with shape by Early (alpha=1.0)\n")
    
  } else if (viz_params$early_point_fill_color) {
    p <- p + 
      geom_tippoint(
        aes(fill = Early),
        size = viz_params$tip_point_size,
        shape = 21,
        color = "black",
        alpha = 1.0
      ) +
      scale_fill_manual(
        values = viz_params$early_colors,
        name = "Early Diverging"
      )
    cat("✅ Tip points with color by Early (alpha=1.0)\n")
  }
  
} else {
  # Without Early metadata
  p <- p + 
    geom_tippoint(
      size = viz_params$tip_point_size,
      color = "black",
      fill = viz_params$tip_point_color,
      shape = 21,
      alpha = 1.0
    )
  cat("✅ Simple tip points (alpha=1.0)\n")
}

#############################################
### STEP 7: Add tip labels with Kingdom options
#############################################
# Applies text coloring or background based on configuration

# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# OPTION 3: Text color by Kingdom
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
if (viz_params$use_metadata && 
    viz_params$kingdom_color_text && 
    !viz_params$kingdom_background_text) {
  p <- p + 
    geom_tiplab(
      aes(color = Kingdom),
      size = viz_params$tip_size,
      align = viz_params$align_tips,
      offset = viz_params$label_offset,
      hjust = 0
    ) +
    scale_color_manual(
      values = viz_params$kingdom_colors,
      name = "Kingdom",
      na.value = "black"
    )
  cat("✓ Tip labels with text color by Kingdom\n")

# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# OPTION 4: Text background by Kingdom
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
} else if (viz_params$use_metadata && 
           viz_params$kingdom_background_text && 
           !viz_params$kingdom_color_text) {
  p <- p + 
    geom_tiplab(
      aes(fill = Kingdom),
      size = viz_params$tip_size,
      align = viz_params$align_tips,
      offset = viz_params$label_offset,
      hjust = 0,
      color = "black",      # Black text
      geom = "label",       # Use label for background
      label.padding = unit(0.15, "lines"),
      label.size = 0        # No border
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = viz_params$kingdom_colors,
      name = "Kingdom",
      na.value = "black"
    )
  cat("✓ Tip labels with background color by Kingdom\n")

# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# No Kingdom coloring (black text, transparent background)
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
} else {
  p <- p + 
    geom_tiplab(
      size = viz_params$tip_size,
      align = viz_params$align_tips,
      offset = viz_params$label_offset,
      hjust = 0,
      color = "black"
    )
  cat("✓ Tip labels with standard format (black)\n")
}

#############################################
### STEP 8: Add Kingdom Lateral Strip
#############################################

if (viz_params$use_metadata && 
    viz_params$show_strip_kingdom &&
    viz_params$metadata_kingdom_column %in% colnames(tree_with_metadata)) {
  
  cat("\n📊 Adding Kingdom lateral strip...\n")
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # STEP 1: Create Kingdom mapping from tree_with_metadata
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  
  # Extract Kingdom mapping
  kingdom_strip_map <- setNames(
    tree_with_metadata[[viz_params$metadata_kingdom_column]],
    tree_with_metadata$clean_label_final  # ✅ Uses clean_label_final
  )
  
  # Verify Kingdom mapping
  cat("  Verificando mapeo Kingdom...\n")
  cat("    Total tips en árbol:", length(tree$tip.label), "\n")
  cat("    Tips con Kingdom asignado:", sum(!is.na(kingdom_strip_map)), "\n")
  cat("    Tips sin Kingdom:", sum(is.na(kingdom_strip_map)), "\n")

  # Show Kingdom distribution
  kingdom_counts <- table(kingdom_strip_map, useNA = "ifany")
  cat("  Distribución de Kingdoms:\n")
  print(kingdom_counts)
  cat("\n")

  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # STEP 2: Extract data from p$data and apply mapping
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  
  strip_kingdom_data <- p$data %>%
    dplyr::filter(isTip) %>%
    dplyr::select(label) %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(label) & label != "") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      label_base = stringr::str_remove(label, " \\[.*\\]$"),
      value = dplyr::coalesce(
        kingdom_strip_map[label],
        kingdom_strip_map[label_base]
      )
    )
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # STEP 3: Verify that we have valid data
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  
  # Verify that all kingdoms have a color assigned
  unique_kingdoms_in_data <- unique(strip_kingdom_data$value[!is.na(strip_kingdom_data$value)])
  missing_colors <- setdiff(unique_kingdoms_in_data, names(viz_params$kingdom_colors))

  if (length(missing_colors) > 0) {
    cat("  ⚠️  WARNING: These Kingdoms don't have colors assigned:\n")
    cat("     ", paste(missing_colors, collapse = ", "), "\n")
    cat("     They will appear BLACK in the strip\n\n")
  }

  # Show Kingdom colors to be used
  cat("  Kingdom colors to be used:\n")
  for (k in unique_kingdoms_in_data) {
    color_hex <- viz_params$kingdom_colors[k]
    if (is.na(color_hex)) color_hex <- "BLACK (missing!)"
    cat("    ", k, "→", color_hex, "\n")
  }
  cat("\n")

  if (nrow(strip_kingdom_data) == 0) {
    cat("  ⚠️  Warning: No Kingdom data available for strip\n")
    cat("     Skipping Kingdom strip\n")
    
  } else if (sum(!is.na(strip_kingdom_data$value)) == 0) {
    cat("  ⚠️  Warning: All Kingdom values are NA\n")
    cat("     Skipping Kingdom strip\n")
    
  } else {
    
  # ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # STEP 4: Calculate offset base
  # ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  
  if (viz_params$show_strip_kingdom) {
    
    if (viz_params$strip_kingdom_offset_mode == "dynamic") {
      # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      # MODO PHYLOGRAM: Offset based on maximum distance from tips
      # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      
      # Estimate average width of labels (more conservative)
      avg_label_length <- mean(nchar(tree$tip.label))
      estimated_label_width <- avg_label_length / 120
      
      # Offset = label_offset + estimated width + small padding
      base_offset_kingdom <- viz_params$label_offset + 
                             estimated_label_width + 
                             viz_params$strip_kingdom_offset_padding
    } else {
      # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      # CLADOGRAM MODE: Fixed offset (original method)
      # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      
      estimated_label_width <- (viz_params$strip_kingdom_fixed_max_chars * 
                                viz_params$tip_size) / 12
      
      base_offset_kingdom <- viz_params$label_offset + 
                             estimated_label_width + 
                             viz_params$strip_kingdom_offset_padding
    }
  }
    
  # ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # STEP 5: Add strip to plot
  # ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  
  p <- p + 
    ggnewscale::new_scale_fill() +  # 🔴 CRITICAL: Reset fill scale
    ggtreeExtra::geom_fruit(
      data = strip_kingdom_data,
      geom = geom_tile,
      mapping = aes(y = label, x = 1, fill = value),  # ✅ Uses 'value'
      width = viz_params$strip_kingdom_width,
      offset = base_offset_kingdom,
      pwidth = 0.1,
      axis.params = list(
        axis = "x",
        text.size = 0,
        line.size = 0
      )
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = viz_params$kingdom_colors,
      name = viz_params$strip_kingdom_label,
      na.value = "black",
      na.translate = TRUE,
      breaks = names(viz_params$kingdom_colors),
      drop = FALSE
    )
  
  # Save total width for subsequent strips
  strip_kingdom_total_width <- viz_params$strip_kingdom_width + 
                               viz_params$strip_kingdom_offset
    
  cat("✅ Kingdom strip added successfully\n")
  cat("  • Width:", viz_params$strip_kingdom_width, "\n")
  cat("  • Offset:", base_offset_kingdom, "\n")
  cat("  • Tips with Kingdom:", sum(!is.na(strip_kingdom_data$value)), 
      "/", nrow(strip_kingdom_data), "\n\n")
  }
  
} else if (viz_params$show_strip_kingdom && !viz_params$use_metadata) {
  cat("⚠️  Kingdom strip requested but metadata disabled\n")
}

# #############################################

#############################################
### STEP 9: Add lateral strip (Ecological Category)
#############################################

if (viz_params$show_strip_considered && 
    viz_params$strip_considered_column %in% colnames(tree_with_metadata)) {
  
  cat("\n📊 Adding Considered (Ecological Category) strip...\n")
  
  # ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # STEP 1: Create mapping from metadata
  # ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  strip_considered_map <- setNames(
    tree_with_metadata[[viz_params$strip_considered_column]],
    tree_with_metadata$clean_label_final
  )
  
  # ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # STEP 2: Extract data from p$data (synchronized)
  # ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  strip_considered_data <- p$data %>%
    dplyr::filter(isTip) %>%
    dplyr::select(label) %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(label) & label != "") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      value = strip_considered_map[label]
    )
  
  # ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # STEP 3: Verify we have valid data
  # ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  
  if (nrow(strip_considered_data) == 0) {
    cat("  ⚠️  Warning: No Considered data available for strip\n")
    cat("     Skipping Considered strip\n")
    
  } else if (sum(!is.na(strip_considered_data$value)) == 0) {
    cat("  ⚠️  Warning: All Considered values are NA\n")
    cat("     Skipping Considered strip\n")
    
  } else {
    
    # ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # STEP 4: Calculate cumulative offset
    # ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    
    if (exists("base_offset_kingdom") && viz_params$show_strip_kingdom) {
      # Si ya existe Kingdom strip, usar su offset como base
      cumulative_offset <- base_offset_kingdom + 
                           viz_params$strip_kingdom_width + 
                           viz_params$strip_considered_offset
      
    } else if (viz_params$strip_kingdom_offset_mode == "dynamic") {
      # Modo phylogram SIN Kingdom strip previo
      tip_data <- p$data %>%
        dplyr::filter(isTip) %>%
        dplyr::select(label, x)
      
      max_tip_distance <- max(tip_data$x, na.rm = TRUE)
      max_label_length <- max(nchar(tree$tip.label))
      estimated_label_width <- (max_label_length * viz_params$tip_size) / 15
      
      cumulative_offset <- max_tip_distance + 
                           estimated_label_width + 
                           viz_params$strip_considered_offset
      
    } else {
      # Modo cladogram SIN Kingdom strip previo
      max_label_length <- max(nchar(tree$tip.label))
      estimated_label_width <- (max_label_length * viz_params$tip_size) / 15
      cumulative_offset <- viz_params$label_offset + 
                           estimated_label_width + 
                           viz_params$strip_considered_offset
    }
    
    cat("  📏 Considered strip offset:", round(cumulative_offset, 2), "\n")
    
    # ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # STEP 5: Add strip to plot
    # ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    
    p <- p + 
      ggnewscale::new_scale_fill() +  # 🔴 CRITICAL: Reset fill scale
      ggtreeExtra::geom_fruit(
        data = strip_considered_data,
        geom = geom_tile,
        mapping = aes(y = label, x = 1, fill = value),
        width = viz_params$strip_considered_width,
        offset = cumulative_offset,
        pwidth = 0.1,
        axis.params = list(
          axis = "x",
          text.size = 0,
          line.size = 0
        )
      ) +
      scale_fill_manual(
        values = viz_params$strip_considered_colors,
        name = viz_params$strip_considered_label,
        na.value = "black",
        na.translate = TRUE
      )
    
    # Save total width for future strips (if needed)
    strip_considered_total_width <- viz_params$strip_considered_width + 
                                     viz_params$strip_considered_offset
    
    cat("✅ Considered strip added successfully\n")
    cat("  • Width:", viz_params$strip_considered_width, "\n")
    cat("  • Offset:", cumulative_offset, "\n")
    cat("  • Tips with category:", sum(!is.na(strip_considered_data$value)), 
        "/", nrow(strip_considered_data), "\n\n")
  }
  
} else if (viz_params$show_strip_considered && !viz_params$use_metadata) {
  cat("⚠️  Considered strip requested but metadata disabled\n")
}


#############################################
### STEP 10: Highlight Specific Clades
#############################################

if (viz_params$highlight_clades && length(viz_params$highlight_genera) > 0) {
  # Find tips matching highlight genera
  for (genus in viz_params$highlight_genera) {
    # Get tips that start with genus name
    highlight_tips <- tree$tip.label[grepl(paste0("^", genus), tree$tip.label)]
    
    # if (length(highlight_tips) > 0) {
    # Find MRCA (Most Recent Common Ancestor) of highlighted tips
    mrca_node <- getMRCA(tree, highlight_tips)
      
    if (!is.null(mrca_node)) {
       p <- p + geom_hilight(
         node = mrca_node,
         fill = viz_params$highlight_color,
         alpha = viz_params$highlight_alpha
      )
    cat("✓ Clade highlighted:", genus, "(node", mrca_node, ")\n")
    }
  }
}

#############################################
### STEP 11: Final Layout Adjustments
#############################################

# Expand plotting area to prevent label cutoff
p <- p + hexpand(10) + vexpand(10)

# Add title
p <- p + ggtitle(
  paste("Phylogenetic Tree -", 
        tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(input_file)))
) + theme(
  plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5)
)

# Add scale bar if requested
if (viz_params$add_scale_bar) {
  p <- p + geom_treescale(
    x = 0,
    y = 0,
    width = 0.5,
    offset = 1,
    fontsize = 3,
    linesize = 0.5,
    color = "black"
  )
  cat("✓ Scale bar added\n")
}

#############################################
### STEP 12: Verification Phylum Annotations
###############################VALIDACIÓN: Verific##############

if (viz_params$show_phylum_labels && exists("tree")) {
  
  cat("\n╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗\n")
  cat("║            PHYLUM ANNOTATION VERIFICATION                 ║\n")
  cat("╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝\n\n")
  
  # Verify that labels have [Abb] annotations
  labels_with_phylum <- grepl("\\[.+\\]$", tree$tip.label)
  n_annotated <- sum(labels_with_phylum)
  n_total <- length(tree$tip.label)
  
  cat("📊 Annotation status:\n")
  cat("  • Tips with Phylum:", n_annotated, "/", n_total, "\n")
  cat("  • Coverage:", round(n_annotated/n_total*100, 1), "%\n\n")
  
  # Show some examples
  cat("📝 Sample annotated labels (first 5):\n")
  sample_labels <- head(tree$tip.label[labels_with_phylum], 5)
  for (i in seq_along(sample_labels)) {
    cat("  ", i, ". ", sample_labels[i], "\n", sep = "")
  }
  
  # Show legend
  cat("\n")
  print_phylum_legend(tree)
  
  cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n")
}

# Display tree
print(p)
cat("\n✓ Tree visualization completed successfully\n")
```

# 9. Export High-Quality Figures

```{r export}
#############################################
### FIGURE EXPORT WORKFLOW
#############################################
# Exports phylogenetic tree in multiple formats for different use cases:
#
# PRIMARY OUTPUTS:
#   1. SVG (Scalable Vector Graphics)
#      - Infinite resolution scaling
#      - Ideal for publication and post-processing
#      - Editable in Adobe Illustrator, Inkscape
#      - Small file size
#
#   2. PNG (Portable Network Graphics)
#      - Raster format with high DPI
#      - Universal compatibility (PowerPoint, Word, web)
#      - Transparent background support
#      - Higher file size but widely supported
#
# OPTIONAL OUTPUTS:
#   3. Separate legend file (SVG)
#      - For multi-panel figures
#      - Allows independent legend positioning
#
#   4. Phylum legend documentation (TSV, TXT, PDF)
#      - For manuscript figure captions
#      - Reference tables for abbreviations

#############################################
### EXPORT 1: Vector Format (SVG)
#############################################
# SVG is the preferred format for scientific publications because:
#   - Resolution-independent (scales infinitely without quality loss)
#   - Text remains editable and searchable
#   - Small file size compared to high-res raster images
#   - Can be imported into illustration software for final touches
#   - Meets journal requirements for vector graphics

cat("\n╔════════════════════════════════════════╗\n")
cat("║       EXPORTING FIGURES                ║\n")
cat("╚════════════════════════════════════════╝\n\n")

cat("📊 Exporting SVG (vector format)...\n")

ggsave(
  filename = export_params$output_svg,
  plot = p,
  device = svglite,                          # svglite package for high-quality SVG
  width = export_params$width,               # figure width in inches
  height = export_params$height,             # figure height in inches
  units = "in"                               # measurement units
)

cat("✅ SVG exported successfully\n")
cat("   File:", export_params$output_svg, "\n")
cat("   Size:", export_params$width, "×", export_params$height, "inches\n")
cat("   Use for: Publication, Illustrator editing\n\n")

#############################################
### EXPORT 2: Raster Format (PNG)
#############################################
# PNG is exported for situations requiring raster graphics:
#   - Presentations (PowerPoint, Keynote)
#   - Word documents and reports
#   - Web display and social media
#   - Quick previews without vector software
#
# DPI (dots per inch) determines output quality:
#   - 72-96 DPI: Screen display, web use
#   - 150 DPI: Draft quality printing
#   - 300 DPI: Standard publication quality (RECOMMENDED)
#   - 600+ DPI: High-end publication, large prints

cat("🖼️  Exporting PNG (raster format)...\n")

ggsave(
  filename = export_params$output_png,
  plot = p,
  device = "png",                            # PNG device (base R)
  width = export_params$width,
  height = export_params$height,
  units = "in",
  dpi = export_params$dpi                    # resolution in dots per inch
)

cat("✅ PNG exported successfully\n")
cat("   File:", export_params$output_png, "\n")
cat("   Size:", export_params$width, "×", export_params$height, "inches\n")
cat("   Resolution:", export_params$dpi, "DPI\n")
cat("   Use for: PowerPoint, Word, web display\n\n")

#############################################
### EXPORT 3: Separate Legend (Optional)
#############################################
# Exports legend as standalone file for advanced figure composition
#
# Use cases:
#   - Multi-panel figures with shared legend
#   - Custom legend placement outside main figure
#   - Figure panels submitted separately to journals
#   - Flexible layout design in Illustrator/Inkscape
#
# The legend is extracted as a separate grob (graphical object)
# and saved with dimensions optimized for standalone use

if (viz_params$use_metadata && viz_params$show_metadata_legend) {
  
  cat("🎨 Exporting separate legend...\n")
  
  # Extract legend as independent graphical object
  legend <- cowplot::get_legend(p)
  
  # Export legend as SVG (vector format for quality)
  ggsave(
    filename = export_params$output_legend,
    plot = legend,
    device = svglite,
    width = 3,                               # narrower width for legend
    height = 4,                              # height adjusted for legend content
    units = "in"
  )
  
  cat("✅ Legend exported successfully\n")
  cat("   File:", export_params$output_legend, "\n")
  cat("   Size: 3×4 inches (optimized for legend)\n")
  cat("   Use for: Multi-panel figures, custom layouts\n\n")
}

#############################################
### EXPORT 4: Phylum Legend Documentation (Optional)
#############################################
# Exports Phylum abbreviation reference in multiple formats
#
# Generated files:
#   1. TSV: Machine-readable table for spreadsheets (Excel, R, Python)
#   2. TXT: Human-readable formatted text for copy-paste to manuscripts
#   3. PDF: Visual reference table for presentations/supplementary materials
#
# These files are essential for:
#   - Figure captions (explaining [Abb] annotations)
#   - Supplementary materials
#   - Collaborator reference
#   - Future reuse and reproducibility

if (viz_params$show_phylum_labels && !is.null(attr(tree, "phylum_legend"))) {
  
  cat("📚 Exporting Phylum legend documentation...\n")
  
  # Export in all three formats
  legend_files <- export_phylum_legend_to_file(
    tree = tree,
    output_dir = output_dir,
    gene_name = file
  )
  
  cat("\n✅ Phylum legend exported in 3 formats:\n")
  cat("   1. TSV (spreadsheet):", basename(legend_files$tsv), "\n")
  cat("      → Import in Excel/R for data analysis\n")
  cat("   2. TXT (formatted):", basename(legend_files$txt), "\n")
  cat("      → Copy to figure caption in manuscript\n")
  cat("   3. PDF (visual):", basename(legend_files$pdf), "\n")
  cat("      → Reference table for presentations\n\n")
}

#############################################
### EXPORT SUMMARY
#############################################

cat("╔════════════════════════════════════════╗\n")
cat("║    EXPORT COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY       ║\n")
cat("╚════════════════════════════════════════╝\n\n")

cat("📁 Output directory:", output_dir, "\n\n")

cat("📊 Files generated:\n")
cat("   ✓ Main figure (SVG):", basename(export_params$output_svg), "\n")
cat("   ✓ Main figure (PNG):", basename(export_params$output_png), "\n")

if (viz_params$use_metadata && viz_params$show_metadata_legend) {
  cat("   ✓ Separate legend:", basename(export_params$output_legend), "\n")
}

if (viz_params$show_phylum_labels && !is.null(attr(tree, "phylum_legend"))) {
  cat("   ✓ Phylum legend (3 formats)\n")
}

cat("\n💡 Next steps:\n")
cat("   1. Review SVG file in vector editor (Illustrator/Inkscape)\n")
cat("   2. Use PNG for presentations and documents\n")
cat("   3. Include Phylum legend in figure caption\n")
cat("   4. Check file sizes and quality before submission\n\n")
```

# 10. Generate Presence/Absence Tables

```{r presence_absence}
#############################################
### INDIVIDUAL GENE TABLE GENERATION
#############################################
# Creates binary matrix showing which organisms contain this gene
#
# This workflow generates ONLY individual gene tables
# The consolidated table is generated by the batch processing script
#
# Individual gene table format:
#   - One table per gene analyzed
#   - Shows which organisms have this specific gene
#   - Includes metadata (Kingdom, Phylum, TaxID, UniProt ID)
#   - Format: TSV file with TRUE/FALSE values
#   - Location: phylogenetic/{hormone}/09_presence-absence/{gene}.tsv

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Check if table generation is enabled
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

if (generate_presence_absence) {
  
  cat("\n╔═══════════════════════════════════════╗\n")
  cat("║   GENERATING GENE TABLE               ║\n")
  cat("╚═══════════════════════════════════════╝\n\n")
  
  cat("📊 Table generation parameters:\n")
  cat("   Hormone category:", hormone, "\n")
  cat("   Current gene:", file, "\n")
  cat("   Output directory:", presence_absence_dir, "\n\n")
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Verify metadata availability
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  
  if (!exists("metadata") || is.null(metadata)) {
    cat("⚠️  Warning: Metadata not loaded. Attempting to load now...\n")
    
    if (file.exists(metadata_file)) {
      metadata <- load_metadata(metadata_file)
      cat("✓ Metadata loaded successfully\n\n")
    } else {
      cat("❌ ERROR: Cannot generate table without metadata file.\n")
      cat("   Expected location:", metadata_file, "\n")
      cat("   Skipping table generation.\n\n")
      generate_presence_absence <- FALSE
    }
  }
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Generate Individual Gene Table
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  
  if (generate_presence_absence && exists("metadata")) {
    
    cat("🧬 Generating table for gene:", file, "\n")
    
    # Generate table with full metadata integration
    presence_table <- generate_presence_absence_table(
      tree_tips = tree$tip.label,
      metadata = metadata,
      tree_with_metadata = tree_with_metadata,
      gene_name = file,
      output_file = presence_absence_file
    )
    
    cat("\n✅ Individual gene table created successfully\n")
    cat("   Location:", presence_absence_file, "\n")
    cat("   Organisms:", nrow(presence_table), "\n\n")
    
    # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    # Information about consolidated table
    # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    
    cat("ℹ️  Consolidated table generation:\n")
    cat("   Individual gene tables are created by this script\n")
    cat("   The consolidated table (merged-genes.tsv) is created by:\n")
    cat("     • The batch processing script (phylogenetic-tree_batch.R)\n")
    cat("     • After all genes have been processed\n")
    cat("     • Location: phylogenetic/", hormone, "/merged-genes.tsv\n\n", sep = "")
  }
  
} else {
  cat("\n⏭️  Table generation skipped\n")
  cat("   Reason: 'generate_presence_absence' = FALSE\n")
  cat("   To enable: Set generate_presence_absence = TRUE\n\n")
}
```

# Appendix: Parameter Guide

## Quick Reference for Common Adjustments

### Making Bootstrap More/Less Prominent

```r
# SUBTLE (publication style)
viz_params$bootstrap_size <- 1.8
viz_params$bootstrap_color <- "#424242"  # Dark gray
viz_params$bootstrap_nudge_x <- 0        # Automatic positioning

# PROMINENT (presentation style)
viz_params$bootstrap_size <- 2.5
viz_params$bootstrap_color <- "firebrick"  # Red
viz_params$bootstrap_nudge_x <- -0.05      # Move toward center
```

### Adjusting Tree Size for Different Taxa Counts

```r
# SMALL TREES (< 30 taxa)
viz_params$tip_size <- 3.0
viz_params$bootstrap_size <- 2.5
viz_params$branch_length_size <- 2.3
viz_params$tip_point_size <- 3.0
viz_params$center_circle_size <- -0.05

# LARGE TREES (> 100 taxa)
viz_params$tip_size <- 1.8
viz_params$bootstrap_size <- 1.5
viz_params$branch_length_size <- 1.6
viz_params$tip_point_size <- 1.2
viz_params$center_circle_size <- -0.15
```

### Color Scheme Alternatives

```r
# GRAYSCALE (for B&W publications)
viz_params$branch_color <- "black"
viz_params$bootstrap_color <- "gray30"
viz_params$branch_length_color <- "gray50"
viz_params$tip_point_color <- "gray20"
viz_params$node_point_color <- "gray40"

# HIGH CONTRAST (for presentations)
viz_params$bootstrap_color <- "#E74C3C"  # Bright red
viz_params$branch_length_color <- "#3498DB"  # Bright blue
```

### Understanding `nudge_x` for Bootstrap

```r
# VALUE GUIDE:
# nudge_x = 0    : Automatic (RECOMMENDED) - positions at node center
# nudge_x = -0.1 : Far toward tree center (may overlap with branches)
# nudge_x = -0.05: Moderate toward center (good for dense trees)
# nudge_x = -0.02: Slight toward center (subtle adjustment)
# nudge_x = 0.02 : Slight toward tips
# nudge_x = 0.05 : Moderate toward tips (may overlap with labels)
```
